questions.stem: What is characteristic of the free-enterprise system?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Public ownership of resources and most economic decisions made by private individuals

choices.label: B
choices.text: Public ownership of resources and most economic decisions made by government planning

choices.label: C
choices.text: Public and private ownership of resources and decisions made by resource owners

choices.label: D
choices.text: Private ownership of resources and decisions made by resource owners

questions.explanation: Free enterprise rests on private ownership of the means of production, with the owners of those resources deciding what to produce and how. Public ownership or central planning is the defining feature of the alternative systems.
questions.explanationJa: 自由企業体制は生産手段の私的所有を基礎とし、その資源の所有者が何をどう生産するかを決める。公的所有や中央計画は、これとは別の体制を特徴づけるものである。

questions.stem: The demand curve for an inferior good is

choices.label: A
choices.text: Downward sloping because of income and substitution effects of price changes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Downward sloping because of increasing marginal utility

choices.label: C
choices.text: Horizontal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Upward sloping because higher prices indicate higher quality

questions.explanation: Even for an inferior good the demand curve slopes downward. A price rise makes the good expensive relative to substitutes, so buyers switch away, and that substitution effect outweighs the perverse income effect. Only a Giffen good, a theoretical extreme, slopes upward.
questions.explanationJa: 下級財であっても需要曲線は右下がりである。価格が上がれば代替財に比べて割高になるので買手は他へ移り、この代替効果が逆向きの所得効果を上回る。右上がりになるのはギッフェン財という理論上の極端な場合だけである。

questions.stem:
The price of good X increases, causing the demand for good Y to decrease. Goods X and Y most likely are
Complements | Substitutes

choices.label: A
choices.text: No | No

choices.label: B
choices.text: No | Yes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes | Yes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes | No

questions.explanation: Goods consumed together are complements: when one becomes dearer, people buy less of the pair, so demand for the other falls. Substitutes work the opposite way, since a dearer X would push buyers toward Y and raise its demand.
questions.explanationJa: 一緒に消費される財は補完財である。一方が高くなれば人々はその組合せ自体を減らすので、他方の需要も落ちる。代替財では逆で、Xが高くなれば買手はYへ移り、Yの需要は増える。

questions.stem: Two goods, Alpha and Beta, are substitutes. What will an increase in the price of Beta cause?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The demand curve for Alpha to shift left

choices.label: B
choices.text: The demand curve for Alpha to shift right

choices.label: C
choices.text: The supply curve for Alpha to shift left

choices.label: D
choices.text: The supply curve for Alpha to shift right

questions.explanation: Beta becoming dearer sends buyers to Alpha, so more Alpha is wanted at every price and the demand curve shifts right. Nothing has happened to the cost of producing Alpha, so its supply curve does not move.
questions.explanationJa: Betaが高くなれば買手はAlphaへ移るので、あらゆる価格水準でAlphaの需要量が増え、需要曲線は右へシフトする。Alphaの生産コストには何も起きていないので、供給曲線は動かない。

questions.stem: When income in Payor City increases, the residents buy more fish and less chicken. Which of the following is an attribute of chicken in Payor?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inferior good

choices.label: B
choices.text: Normal good

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perfectly inelastic demand

choices.label: D
choices.text: Relatively elastic demand

questions.explanation: An inferior good is one people buy less of as they grow richer, because they can now afford something they prefer. Chicken behaves exactly that way here. Note that this says nothing about elasticity, which concerns the response to price rather than to income.
questions.explanationJa: 下級財とは、豊かになるにつれて購入量が減る財である。より好ましいものを買えるようになるからである。ここでの鶏肉はまさにその挙動を示している。なおこれは弾力性とは無関係である。弾力性は所得ではなく価格への反応を扱う概念である。

questions.stem: Demand for peanut oil formerly rose and fell directly with changes in income, but now varies inversely with income, despite price increases. What change is the most likely explanation for this shift?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Boycott by consumers protesting industry practices

choices.label: B
choices.text: Expectation of deflation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase in income

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change in preferences

questions.explanation: The good has changed category, from normal to inferior, and that classification is a property of consumers' tastes. A rise in income moves along the existing relationship rather than reversing its direction, so only a change in preferences explains the reversal.
questions.explanationJa: この財は通常財から下級財へと分類が変わっており、この分類は消費者の嗜好の性質である。所得の増加は既存の関係の上を移動するだけで、その向きを反転させはしない。したがって反転を説明できるのは嗜好の変化だけである。

questions.stem:
How do the quantity supplied and demanded relate to price changes?
Supplied | Demanded

choices.label: A
choices.text: Inversely | Directly

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inversely | Inversely

choices.label: C
choices.text: Directly | Inversely

choices.label: D
choices.text: Directly | Directly

questions.explanation: Higher prices make production more profitable, so sellers offer more: supply varies directly with price. Higher prices make buying more costly, so buyers take less: demand varies inversely with price. The two opposing responses are what produce an equilibrium.
questions.explanationJa: 価格が上がれば生産の採算が良くなるので売手はより多く供給する。供給量は価格と正の関係にある。価格が上がれば購入の負担が増すので買手はより少なく買う。需要量は価格と逆の関係にある。この相反する2つの反応が均衡を生む。

questions.stem: The supply curve for a normal good is

choices.label: A
choices.text: Downward sloping because of income and substitution effects of price changes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Downward sloping because of increasing marginal utility

choices.label: C
choices.text: Horizontal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Upward sloping because entities produce more at higher prices

questions.explanation: Supply slopes upward because a higher price covers the rising marginal cost of extra output, so producers are willing to make more. The reasoning in choices A and B belongs to the demand side.
questions.explanationJa: 供給曲線が右上がりになるのは、価格が高ければ追加生産に伴って上昇する限界費用を賄えるため、生産者がより多く作ろうとするからである。選択肢AとBが述べている理屈は需要側のものである。

questions.stem: Young and Zeta are substitute goods. What would cause a shift in the supply curve to the right for Young, a normal good?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cost-saving technological improvements in the production process for Young

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cost-saving technological improvements in the production process for Zeta

choices.label: C
choices.text: An expected increase in the future price of Young

choices.label: D
choices.text: An increase in the price paid for Zeta

questions.explanation: Supply shifts when the cost of producing the good itself changes. Cheaper technology for Young lowers its cost at every output level, so more is offered at each price. The other three would move Young's demand curve, or Zeta's supply, not Young's supply.
questions.explanationJa: 供給曲線がシフトするのは、その財自体の生産コストが変わるときである。Youngの生産技術が安価になれば、どの産出水準でもコストが下がるので、各価格でより多く供給される。他の3つはYoungの需要曲線かZetaの供給曲線を動かすものであって、Youngの供給曲線ではない。

questions.stem:
Bob Bounce has two job offers: one as an accountant and one as a basketball player. He would accept either job for $50,000 annually. Due to his basketball skills, he is offered $500,000 as a basketball player.
The $450,000 difference is called

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cross elasticity of demand

choices.label: B
choices.text: Economic rent

choices.label: C
choices.text: Equilibrium price

choices.label: D
choices.text: Marginal cost

questions.explanation: Economic rent is the excess of what a resource actually earns over the minimum it would have accepted, which is its opportunity cost. Bob would have played for $50,000, so the extra $450,000 is rent arising from a skill in scarce supply.
questions.explanationJa: 経済的レント（economic rent）とは、ある資源が実際に得る報酬が、それを受け入れる最低額、すなわち機会費用を超える部分をいう。Bobは $50,000 でも働いたはずなので、上乗せの $450,000 は希少な技能から生じるレントである。

questions.stem: In which of the following situations would there be inelastic demand?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A 5 percent price increase results in a 3 percent decrease in the quantity demanded.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A 4 percent price increase results in a 6 percent decrease in the quantity demanded.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A 4 percent price increase results in a 4 percent decrease in the quantity demanded.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A 3 percent price decrease results in a 5 percent increase in the quantity demanded.

questions.explanation: Demand is inelastic when quantity responds proportionally less than price, that is, when the elasticity is below 1. Only choice A does this: 3% / 5% = 0.6. Choice C is unit elastic, and B and D are elastic.
questions.explanationJa: 需要が非弾力的であるとは、数量の反応が価格の変化に比べて比例的に小さいこと、すなわち弾力性が1を下回ることをいう。これに該当するのは選択肢Aだけである: 3% ÷ 5% = 0.6。選択肢Cは単位弾力的、BとDは弾力的である。

questions.stem: Which of the following characteristics would indicate that an item sold would have a high price elasticity of demand?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The item has many similar substitutes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cost of the item is low compared to the total budget of the purchasers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The item is considered a necessity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Changes in the price of the item are regulated by governmental agency.

questions.explanation: Elasticity is high when buyers can easily walk away, and the availability of close substitutes is the strongest single determinant. A necessity, a small share of the budget, and regulated pricing all make demand less responsive, not more.
questions.explanationJa: 弾力性が高くなるのは、買手が容易に離れられるときであり、近い代替財があるかどうかが最も強い決定要因である。必需品であること、家計に占める割合が小さいこと、価格が規制されていることは、いずれも需要の反応を鈍くする方向に働く。

questions.stem: The widgets market is elastic and purely competitive. Barring Company supplies only widgets. The market price of widgets increases. What is the effect on Barring's total revenue?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increases

choices.label: C
choices.text: Indeterminate from the given information

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remains the same

questions.explanation: When demand is elastic, quantity falls proportionally more than the price rises, so the two effects on revenue do not cancel and total revenue falls. This is the general rule: with elastic demand, price and total revenue move in opposite directions.
questions.explanationJa: 需要が弾力的な場合、価格の上昇率よりも数量の減少率の方が大きいので、収入に対する2つの効果は相殺されず、総収入は減少する。これが一般則である。需要が弾力的であれば、価格と総収入は逆方向に動く。

questions.stem:
Fairfield Co. graphed the quantity demanded against price for its three products, X, Y and Z. On the graph, price is on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal axis. Curve Dy is the steepest, Dx is intermediate, and Dz is much the flattest of the three.
Which product has the most price elasticity of demand?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Indeterminate from the given information

choices.label: B
choices.text: X

choices.label: C
choices.text: Y

choices.label: D
choices.text: Z

questions.explanation: The flatter the demand curve, the larger the change in quantity for a given change in price, and therefore the greater the elasticity. Dz is much the flattest of the three, so product Z has the most elastic demand and Y, the steepest, the least.
questions.explanationJa: 需要曲線が緩やかであるほど、同じ価格変化に対する数量の変化が大きく、したがって弾力性も大きい。Dzは3本の中で最も緩やかなので、製品Zの需要が最も弾力的であり、最も急なYが最も非弾力的ということになる。

questions.stem: Coffee and tea are substitutes. What is the most likely result of a widespread coffee boycott?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased demand for coffee

choices.label: B
choices.text: Higher economic profits for coffee producers

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased inelasticity in demand for coffee

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased supply of coffee

questions.explanation: A boycott is a change in tastes, so it shifts the demand curve for coffee to the left: less is wanted at every price. Price and quantity both fall, which reduces producers' profits, and supply is unaffected because nothing has changed in production.
questions.explanationJa: ボイコットは嗜好の変化なので、コーヒーの需要曲線を左へシフトさせる。あらゆる価格で需要量が減るということである。価格も数量も下がり、生産者の利益は減る。生産面には何も変化がないので供給は影響を受けない。

questions.stem:
What effect on output quantity and market price will simultaneous increase in supply and demand have?
Output quantity | Market price

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase | Increase

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase | Indeterminate

choices.label: C
choices.text: Indeterminate | Increase

choices.label: D
choices.text: Indeterminate | Indeterminate

questions.explanation: Both shifts push quantity the same way, so output certainly rises. On price they pull against each other: rising demand lifts it, rising supply depresses it. Without knowing which shift is larger, the net effect on price cannot be determined.
questions.explanationJa: 2つのシフトは数量を同じ方向へ押すので、産出量は確実に増える。価格については互いに逆に働く。需要の増加は押し上げ、供給の増加は押し下げる。どちらのシフトが大きいか分からない限り、価格への正味の影響は定まらない。

questions.stem: A competitive market model of supply and demand predicts a long-run shortage only when

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maximum price is set above the equilibrium price

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maximum price is set below the equilibrium price

choices.label: C
choices.text: Minimum price is set above the equilibrium price

choices.label: D
choices.text: Minimum price is set below the equilibrium price

questions.explanation: A shortage means quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, which persists only if price is prevented from rising to clear the market. A maximum price, or ceiling, set below equilibrium does exactly that. A ceiling above equilibrium is not binding, and a minimum price above equilibrium creates a surplus instead.
questions.explanationJa: 不足（shortage）とは需要量が供給量を上回る状態であり、これが持続するのは、市場を均衡させるところまで価格が上がることを妨げられている場合だけである。均衡価格を下回る上限価格（price ceiling）がまさにそれにあたる。均衡を上回る上限価格は拘束力を持たず、均衡を上回る下限価格は逆に余剰を生む。

questions.stem: Kingston Company is considering replacing its factory's existing equipment with robotic equipment. What is an irrelevant factor in this decision?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The capital-to-labor ratio

choices.label: B
choices.text: Economies of scale

choices.label: C
choices.text: The existing equipment's cost

choices.label: D
choices.text: Opportunity cost

questions.explanation: The existing equipment's original cost is sunk: it has already been paid and no choice now can recover it. What matters is the future, the capital-to-labour trade-off the robots imply, the scale economies they permit, and the opportunity cost of the funds.
questions.explanationJa: 既存設備の取得原価は埋没原価である。既に支払済みであり、今どの選択をしても回収できない。問題になるのは将来のことであり、ロボット化が意味する資本と労働の代替関係、それによって得られる規模の経済、そして資金の機会費用である。

questions.stem: A city ordinance that freezes rent prices may cause

choices.label: A
choices.text: The demand curve for rental space to fall

choices.label: B
choices.text: The supply curve for rental space to rise

choices.label: C
choices.text: Demand for rental space to exceed supply

choices.label: D
choices.text: Supply of rental space to exceed demand

questions.explanation: A rent freeze is a price ceiling. Held below the market rate, it encourages tenants to demand more space while giving landlords no reason to supply it, so quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied and a housing shortage develops.
questions.explanationJa: 家賃の凍結は上限価格の一種である。市場相場を下回る水準で据え置かれると、借手はより広い空間を求める一方、貸手には供給する理由がなくなるので、需要量が供給量を上回り、住宅不足が生じる。

questions.stem: Which of the following statement is correct if there is an increase in the resources available within an economy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: More goods and services will be produced in the economy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The economy will be capable of producing more goods and services.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The standard of living in the economy will rise.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The technological efficiency of the economy will improve.

questions.explanation: More resources expand the production possibilities frontier, so the economy becomes capable of producing more. Whether it actually does depends on whether those resources are employed, and living standards depend on output per person, not on output alone.
questions.explanationJa: 資源が増えれば生産可能性フロンティアが外側へ広がるので、経済はより多く生産できるようになる。実際に生産するかどうかはその資源が雇用されるかによるし、生活水準は産出量そのものではなく1人当たり産出量に依存する。

questions.stem: Which of the following is not characteristic of indifference curves for a two-good economy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are plotted on a graph with the quantities of one good on the x-axis and another good on the y-axis

choices.label: B
choices.text: They are sloped convex to the origin

choices.label: C
choices.text: They are sloped negatively

choices.label: D
choices.text: They shift to the right with an increase in income

questions.explanation: An indifference curve maps combinations of two goods that give equal satisfaction, and that ranking of preferences does not depend on income. What income changes is the budget line, which shifts outward and lets the consumer reach a higher curve that was already there.
questions.explanationJa: 無差別曲線は、同じ満足度を与える2財の組合せを描いたものであり、この選好の順序は所得に依存しない。所得が変えるのは予算線である。予算線が外側へシフトすることで、もともと存在していたより高い無差別曲線に到達できるようになる。

questions.stem: Which of the following examples illustrates the principle of diminishing returns?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bill’s Mowing takes 30 minutes to mow and trim a 5,000 square foot lawn and 45 minutes to mow and trim a 10,000 square foot lawn.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the Maher Inn’s kitchen, three cooks can prepare 150 meals in one evening; four cooks can prepare 180 meals.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A single copy of a 5,000-copy printing of a 120-page paperback and a single copy of a 10-copy printing a 30-page presentation have the same unit cost.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A small furnace is less efficient than a large one.

questions.explanation: Diminishing returns appear when adding a unit of a variable input to fixed inputs yields less extra output than the previous unit did. Three cooks average 50 meals each, but the fourth adds only 30, because the kitchen and equipment are fixed.
questions.explanationJa: 収穫逓減が現れるのは、固定的な投入に対して可変投入を1単位追加したとき、その増加分が前の1単位より小さくなる場合である。3人の料理人は1人当たり50食だが、4人目は30食しか増やさない。厨房と設備が固定されているからである。

questions.stem: What is normal profit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The cost of resources from an economic perspective

choices.label: B
choices.text: Equal to economic profit

choices.label: C
choices.text: Equal to net income prepared in conforming with generally accepted accounting principles

choices.label: D
choices.text: Profit calculated using only explicit costs

questions.explanation: Normal profit is the return just sufficient to keep resources in their present use, so it is the opportunity cost of those resources and an economist counts it as a cost. Economic profit is what remains after it, which is why zero economic profit still means the owner is adequately rewarded.
questions.explanationJa: 正常利潤とは、資源を現在の用途に留めておくのにちょうど足りる報酬であり、その資源の機会費用にあたるため、経済学ではこれを費用として扱う。経済的利潤はそれを差し引いた後に残る部分である。経済的利潤がゼロでも所有者は十分な報酬を得ていることになるのはそのためである。

questions.stem: What is the sum of average variable costs and average fixed costs for a given output?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Average total cost

choices.label: B
choices.text: Economic cost

choices.label: C
choices.text: Explicit costs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Implicit costs

questions.explanation: Average total cost = total cost / output, and since total cost is fixed plus variable, the average splits the same way. Average fixed cost falls continuously as output spreads the fixed cost, while average variable cost eventually rises, which gives average total cost its U shape.
questions.explanationJa: 平均総費用 = 総費用 ÷ 産出量 であり、総費用が固定費と変動費の和である以上、平均も同じように分解できる。平均固定費は産出量の増加とともに固定費が薄まって下がり続け、平均変動費はやがて上昇に転じる。平均総費用がU字型になるのはこのためである。

questions.stem: Clegg Company's average cost is decreasing over a range of increased output. What is Clegg experiencing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreasing fixed costs

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreasing returns

choices.label: C
choices.text: Economies of scale

choices.label: D
choices.text: Technological efficiency

questions.explanation: Economies of scale mean average cost per unit falls as output expands, through specialization, bulk buying, and the spreading of fixed costs. Decreasing returns would push average cost up, and fixed costs do not fall; it is average fixed cost per unit that declines, which is one source of the effect rather than a separate phenomenon.
questions.explanationJa: 規模の経済とは、産出量の拡大につれて単位当たり平均費用が下がることをいい、分業の進展・大量仕入・固定費の分散によって生じる。収穫逓減であれば平均費用は上昇するし、固定費そのものが減るわけでもない。減るのは単位当たり平均固定費であり、これは規模の経済の一因であって別個の現象ではない。

questions.stem: The costs of the use of a resource for the production of one good rather than another are

choices.label: A
choices.text: Economic cost

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fixed costs

choices.label: C
choices.text: Historical costs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Opportunity costs

questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative given up. Using a resource for one good necessarily means not using it for another, and that forgone use is the true economic cost, whatever the accounting records show.
questions.explanationJa: 機会費用とは、断念した最善の代替案の価値である。ある資源をある財の生産に使うことは、必然的に別の財に使わないことを意味し、その放棄された用途こそが真の経済的費用である。会計帳簿に何が記録されるかとは関係しない。

questions.stem: The sprocket market is purely competitive. Searing, a sprocket producer, is considering strategies. Which is the least likely business strategy for Searing to select?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cost leadership

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cost differentiation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Differentiation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Process reengineering

questions.explanation: Pure competition assumes a homogeneous product that buyers regard as identical, so no producer can command a premium by making its version distinctive. Cost-based strategies remain open, since a lower cost still yields profit at the market price.
questions.explanationJa: 純粋競争は、買手が同一とみなす同質の製品を前提とするので、自社の製品を差別化して割増価格を得ることはどの生産者にもできない。コストに基づく戦略は依然として有効である。コストが低ければ市場価格のもとでも利益が残るからである。

questions.stem: Which of the following is an assumption in a perfectly competitive financial market?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No signal trader or traders can have a significant impact on market prices.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some trades can impact market prices more than others.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trading prices vary based on supply only.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Information about borrowing/lending activities is only available to those willing to pay market prices.

questions.explanation: Perfect competition assumes participants are price takers: each is too small relative to the market to move the price, and information is freely available to all. Choices B and D contradict that directly.
questions.explanationJa: 完全競争は、参加者が価格受容者であることを前提とする。各参加者は市場に比べて小さすぎて価格を動かせず、情報は誰にでも自由に入手できる。選択肢BとDはこの前提に真っ向から反する。

questions.stem: How does a company maintain a natural monopoly?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The company owns patents.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The company owns natural resources.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Economic or technological conditions permit only one efficient supplier.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Entry and exit barriers to the market exist.

questions.explanation: A natural monopoly arises where costs fall over the entire relevant range of demand, so one firm can supply the whole market more cheaply than two could. Utilities are the classic case. Patents, resource ownership, and entry barriers create monopolies of other kinds.
questions.explanationJa: 自然独占は、需要の関連範囲全体にわたって費用が低下し続ける場合に生じる。1社が市場全体に供給する方が2社で分けるより安上がりになるためである。公益事業がその典型例である。特許・資源の所有・参入障壁は、別の種類の独占を生む要因である。

questions.stem: Under which of the following conditions is the supplier most able to influence or control buyers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the supplier’s products are not differentiated

choices.label: B
choices.text: When the supplier does not face the threat of substitute products

choices.label: C
choices.text: When the industry is controlled by a large number of companies

choices.label: D
choices.text: When the purchasing industry is an important customer to the supplying industry

questions.explanation: Supplier power is greatest when the buyer has nowhere else to go. If no substitute product threatens the supplier's offering, the buyer must accept its terms. Undifferentiated products, a fragmented supplying industry, and being an important customer all shift power toward the buyer.
questions.explanationJa: 供給業者の交渉力が最も強くなるのは、買手に他の選択肢がないときである。代替品が供給業者の製品を脅かさないのであれば、買手はその条件を受け入れざるを得ない。製品が差別化されていないこと、供給側の業界が多数の企業に分かれていること、買手が重要な顧客であることは、いずれも力関係を買手側へ動かす。

questions.stem: All of the following are components of the formula used to calculate gross domestic product except

choices.label: A
choices.text: Household income

choices.label: B
choices.text: Foreign net export spending

choices.label: C
choices.text: Government spending

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gross investment

questions.explanation: GDP by the expenditure approach is consumption plus gross investment plus government spending plus net exports. Household income belongs to the income approach, which arrives at the same total from the other side, so it is not a term in this formula.
questions.explanationJa: 支出面から見たGDPは、消費 + 総投資 + 政府支出 + 純輸出である。家計所得は分配面（所得アプローチ）に属し、反対側から同じ総額に到達する経路であって、この式の項ではない。

questions.stem: Gross domestic product includes which of the following measures?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The size of a population that must share a given output within one year

choices.label: B
choices.text: The negative externalities of the production process of a nation within one year

choices.label: C
choices.text: The total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a nation in one year

choices.label: D
choices.text: The total monetary value of goods and services including barter transactions within a nation in one year

questions.explanation: GDP is the market value of final goods and services produced within a nation's borders in a year. Intermediate goods are excluded to avoid double counting, and transactions with no market price, such as barter and household production, are omitted, as are externalities.
questions.explanationJa: GDPは、一国の国境内で1年間に生産された最終財・サービスの市場価値である。二重計算を避けるため中間財は除外され、物々交換や家庭内生産のように市場価格の付かない取引も、外部性と同様に算入されない。

questions.stem: An economy is at the peak of the business cycle. Which of the following policy packages is the most effective way to dampen the economy and prevent inflation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase government spending, reduce taxes, increase money supply, and reduce interest rates

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduce government spending, increase taxes, increase money supply, and increase interest rates

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduce government spending, increase taxes, reduce money supply, and increase interest rates

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduce government spending, reduce taxes, reduce money supply, and reduce interest rates

questions.explanation: Dampening an overheating economy calls for both arms of policy to pull the same way. Fiscal restraint means less government spending and higher taxes; monetary restraint means a smaller money supply and higher interest rates. Choices B and D mix a contractionary measure with an expansionary one.
questions.explanationJa: 過熱した経済を冷やすには、財政・金融の両輪を同じ方向に働かせる必要がある。財政の引き締めは政府支出の削減と増税、金融の引き締めはマネーサプライの縮小と金利の引き上げである。選択肢BとDは引き締め策と緩和策を混在させている。

questions.stem: Which of the following strategies would the Federal Reserve most likely pursue under an expansionary policy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Purchase federal securities and lower the discount rate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reduce the reserve requirement while raising the discount rate.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Raise the reserve requirement and lower the discount rate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Raise the reserve requirement and the discount rate.

questions.explanation: Expansion means putting more money into the system. Buying securities on the open market pays cash into banks' reserves, and a lower discount rate makes borrowing from the Fed cheaper. Lowering the reserve requirement would also expand, but no choice pairs it with another expansionary step.
questions.explanationJa: 金融緩和とは、システムにより多くの資金を供給することである。公開市場で証券を買い入れれば銀行の準備預金に現金が入り、公定歩合の引き下げは連邦準備銀行からの借入を安くする。預金準備率の引き下げも緩和にあたるが、それを他の緩和策と組み合わせた選択肢はない。

questions.stem: What factor would explain a low propensity for savings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ownership of a high proportion of liquid assets

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increasing real interest rates

choices.label: C
choices.text: High debt loads

choices.label: D
choices.text: Consumer expectations of future price decreases

questions.explanation: Saving is largely a response to the need for a financial cushion. A household already holding plenty of liquid assets has that cushion and feels little pressure to add to it. Higher real interest rates reward saving, heavy debt forces repayment which is itself saving, and expected price falls encourage postponing purchases.
questions.explanationJa: 貯蓄は主として、金融的な備えを持ちたいという必要への反応である。既に十分な流動資産を持つ家計はその備えがあるので、さらに積み増す圧力をあまり感じない。実質金利の上昇は貯蓄を報い、重い債務は返済を迫るがそれ自体が貯蓄であり、物価下落の予想は購入の先送りを促す。

questions.stem: The multiplier effect explains

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase in autonomous investment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase in induced investments

choices.label: C
choices.text: Multiplied increase in national income due to increases in autonomous investment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Multiplied increase in national income due to increases in induced investment

questions.explanation: An initial injection of autonomous spending becomes income to its recipients, who spend part of it again, and so on. The total rise in national income is therefore a multiple of the original injection, the multiplier being 1 / (1 - MPC). Induced investment responds to income rather than initiating the chain.
questions.explanationJa: 独立的支出の当初の注入は、受け取った人々の所得となり、その一部が再び支出され、これが繰り返される。したがって国民所得の増加総額は当初の注入額の何倍かになり、乗数は 1 ÷ (1 − 限界消費性向) で与えられる。誘発投資は所得に反応するものであって、この連鎖を起こす側ではない。

questions.stem:
Question 39 and 40 are based on the following information about countries Cleo and Elin.
Disposable | Cleo | Elin
Income Level | Consumption | Consumption
$52,000 | $40,000 | $39,000
$28,000 | $24,000 | $27,000
What is Cleo's marginal propensity to save?
questions.explanation: The marginal propensity to save is the share of an extra dollar of income that is not consumed. Income rises $24,000 while consumption rises $16,000, so MPC = 16/24 = 0.67 and MPS = 1 - 0.67 = 0.33. Choice B is the average propensity to save at the higher income level, not the marginal one.
questions.explanationJa: 限界貯蓄性向とは、追加的な所得1ドルのうち消費に回されない割合である。所得が $24,000 増える間に消費は $16,000 増えているので、限界消費性向 = 16 ÷ 24 = 0.67、限界貯蓄性向 = 1 − 0.67 = 0.33。選択肢Bは高い所得水準における平均貯蓄性向であって、限界の値ではない。

questions.stem:
Which country has a higher average propensity to save at each income level?
$52,000 | $28,000

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cleo | Cleo

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cleo | Elin

choices.label: C
choices.text: Elin | Elin

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elin | Cleo

questions.explanation: Average propensity to save = saving / income at that level. At $52,000 Cleo saves $12,000 (0.23) and Elin $13,000 (0.25), so Elin is higher. At $28,000 Cleo saves $4,000 (0.14) and Elin only $1,000 (0.04), so Cleo is higher. Elin saves a larger share when income is high but almost nothing when it is low, which is why the ranking reverses.
questions.explanationJa: 平均貯蓄性向 = その水準における貯蓄 ÷ 所得。$52,000 では Cleo が $12,000（0.23）、Elin が $13,000（0.25）なので Elin が高い。$28,000 では Cleo が $4,000（0.14）、Elin はわずか $1,000（0.04）なので Cleo が高い。Elin は所得が高いときには多くを貯蓄するが低いときにはほとんど貯蓄しない。順位が入れ替わるのはそのためである。

questions.stem: What factor tends to increase investment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A high capital goods stock quantity

choices.label: B
choices.text: A increase in acquisition costs

choices.label: C
choices.text: A low technology growth rate

choices.label: D
choices.text: A real interest rate decrease

questions.explanation: Investment is undertaken when the expected return exceeds the cost of funds. A fall in the real interest rate lowers that hurdle, so projects that were marginal become worthwhile. A large existing capital stock, higher acquisition costs, and slow technological change all discourage investment.
questions.explanationJa: 投資が実行されるのは、期待収益が資金コストを上回るときである。実質金利の低下はそのハードルを引き下げるので、それまで限界的だった案件が採算に乗る。既存の資本ストックが大きいこと、取得コストの上昇、技術進歩の停滞は、いずれも投資を抑制する。

questions.stem: What factor increases when U.S. commercial banks increase net deposits?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Purchasing power of the U.S. dollar

choices.label: B
choices.text: Real U.S. national income

choices.label: C
choices.text: Real wealth of the U.S.

choices.label: D
choices.text: U.S. money supply

questions.explanation: Demand deposits are part of the money supply, so an increase in net deposits at commercial banks increases it directly, and the banks' subsequent lending multiplies the effect. Purchasing power, real income, and real wealth all depend on output and prices rather than on the form in which money is held.
questions.explanationJa: 要求払預金はマネーサプライの一部なので、商業銀行の正味預金が増えればマネーサプライは直接に増加し、その後の銀行の貸出がさらにこれを乗数的に拡大する。購買力・実質所得・実質資産はいずれも産出量と物価に依存するものであって、貨幣がどの形で保有されているかによって決まるものではない。

questions.stem: Which of the following Federal Reserve policies would increase money supply?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the multiplier effect

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase reserve requirements

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reduce the discount rate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sell more U.S. Treasury bonds

questions.explanation: A lower discount rate makes it cheaper for banks to borrow reserves from the Fed, so they hold fewer excess reserves and lend more, expanding the money supply. Raising reserve requirements and selling bonds both drain reserves, and the multiplier is a consequence of the reserve ratio rather than a policy lever.
questions.explanationJa: 公定歩合を引き下げれば、銀行が連邦準備銀行から準備預金を借りるコストが下がるので、超過準備を抱え込まずに貸出を増やし、マネーサプライは拡大する。預金準備率の引き上げと国債の売却はいずれも準備預金を吸収する。乗数は準備率から生じる帰結であって、政策手段ではない。

questions.stem: Carlton Bank has an increase in reserves of $1,000,000. If the reserve ratio is 10%, by what amount may Carlton increase its demand deposits?
questions.explanation: The money multiplier is 1 / reserve ratio = 1 / 0.10 = 10, so $1,000,000 of new reserves can support $10,000,000 of deposits once the banking system has lent and relent the funds. Choice B, $900,000, is what a single bank could lend out immediately from that first deposit.
questions.explanationJa: 信用乗数は 1 ÷ 預金準備率 = 1 ÷ 0.10 = 10 なので、$1,000,000 の新規準備預金は、銀行システム全体が貸出と再貸出を繰り返した後に $10,000,000 の預金を支えうる。選択肢Bの $900,000 は、最初の預金から1行が直ちに貸し出せる金額である。

questions.stem: To address the problem of a recession, the Federal Reserve Bank most likely would take which of the following actions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lower the discount rate it charges to banks for loans

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sell U.S. government bonds in open-market transactions

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the federal funds rate charged by banks when they borrow from one another

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the level of funds a bank is legally required to hold in reserve

questions.explanation: A recession calls for easier money. Lowering the discount rate cheapens bank borrowing from the Fed and encourages lending. The other three are contractionary: selling bonds drains reserves, a higher federal funds rate raises the cost of interbank funds, and a higher reserve requirement locks funds away.
questions.explanationJa: 景気後退期には金融緩和が求められる。公定歩合の引き下げは銀行が連邦準備銀行から借りるコストを下げ、貸出を促す。他の3つは引き締め策である。国債の売却は準備預金を吸収し、フェデラルファンド金利の上昇は銀行間資金のコストを上げ、預金準備率の引き上げは資金を固定してしまう。

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct regarding the consumer price index (CPI) for measuring the estimated decrease in a company's buying power?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The CPI is measured only once every 10 years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The products a company buys should differ from what a consumer buys.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The CPI measures what consumers will pay for items.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The CPI is skewed by foreign currency translations.

questions.explanation: The CPI tracks a basket of goods bought by households, which is not what a business purchases. A company facing rising costs of raw materials and industrial inputs should use a producer price index or an index built for its own basket. The CPI is published monthly, not decennially.
questions.explanationJa: 消費者物価指数（CPI）は家計が購入する財のバスケットを追跡するものであり、企業が購入するものとは異なる。原材料や産業用の投入財のコスト上昇に直面する企業は、生産者物価指数や自社のバスケットに合わせた指数を使うべきである。なおCPIは10年ごとではなく毎月公表される。

questions.stem: Keynesian economic theory holds that during the peak of the business cycle, the normal workings of the labor market result in

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cyclical unemployment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Frictional unemployment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Phillips unemployment

choices.label: D
choices.text: No unemployment

questions.explanation: At the peak, cyclical unemployment has disappeared, but people are always between jobs, entering the workforce, or relocating. That frictional unemployment is unavoidable in any functioning labour market, so full employment never means a zero rate.
questions.explanationJa: 景気の頂点では循環的失業は消えているが、転職の合間にある人、労働市場に参入したばかりの人、転居中の人は常に存在する。この摩擦的失業は機能している労働市場ではどうしても避けられないので、完全雇用が失業率ゼロを意味することはない。

questions.stem: Which classification best applies to the employer's portion of Social Security taxes, from the employee's perspective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Direct

choices.label: B
choices.text: Proportional

choices.label: C
choices.text: Progressive

choices.label: D
choices.text: Regressive

questions.explanation: Social Security tax is levied on wages up to a ceiling, so earnings above that point bear no further tax. The effective rate therefore falls as income rises, which is what regressive means. Economists treat the employer's share as ultimately borne by the employee through lower wages.
questions.explanationJa: 社会保障税は上限額までの賃金に課され、それを超える部分には課税されない。したがって所得が上がるほど実効税率は下がり、これが逆進的（regressive）ということである。経済学では、雇用主負担分も最終的には賃金の抑制を通じて従業員が負担すると考える。

questions.stem: What is the most likely impact of government borrowing to finance deficits that increases the demand for loan funds?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease in the supply of loan funds

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease interest rates

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the ease with which businesses can borrow funds

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase interest rates

questions.explanation: Government borrowing adds to the demand for a limited pool of loanable funds, and greater demand at a given supply raises the price of those funds, which is the interest rate. Private borrowers then find credit dearer and scarcer, the effect known as crowding out.
questions.explanationJa: 政府の借入は、限られた貸付資金への需要を増やす。供給が一定のまま需要が増えれば、その資金の価格すなわち金利は上昇する。その結果、民間の借手にとって信用は高価で入手しにくくなる。これがクラウディングアウトと呼ばれる効果である。

questions.stem: What is the federal budget deficit?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The excess of imports over exports in one year

choices.label: B
choices.text: The excess of federal government spending over revenues in one year

choices.label: C
choices.text: The excess of the federal government’s liabilities over assets on its balance sheet

choices.label: D
choices.text: The cumulative excess of federal government spending over revenues

questions.explanation: The deficit is a flow measured over one year: spending less revenue for that year. The accumulated total of past deficits is the national debt, which is the stock, so choice D confuses the two.
questions.explanationJa: 財政赤字は1年間について測られるフローであり、その年の歳出から歳入を差し引いたものである。過去の赤字を累積した総額は国債残高というストックであり、選択肢Dはこの2つを混同している。

questions.stem: What is a consequence of trade between nations?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Possibility of an increase in total world output

choices.label: B
choices.text: Less variety in consumer products

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tendency for imports to exceed exports

choices.label: D
choices.text: Higher consumer prices

questions.explanation: When each country specializes where its opportunity cost is lowest and trades for the rest, the same resources yield more in total, so world output can rise. Trade also widens the range of goods available and tends to lower prices, and it says nothing about which side of the balance any one country ends up on.
questions.explanationJa: 各国が機会費用の最も低い分野に特化し、残りを貿易で調達すれば、同じ資源からより多くの産出が得られるので、世界全体の生産は増えうる。貿易は入手できる財の種類も広げ、価格を下げる方向に働く。また、どの国が輸出超過になるか輸入超過になるかについては何も含意しない。

questions.stem:
Which statements regarding absolute and comparative advantage are valid?
I. Absolute advantage is the ability of one nation to produce goods at relatively lower opportunity
costs than another nation.
II. International trade allows a nation to specialize in goods that it produces efficiently, while still obtaining goods it doesn't produce.
III. Total global output is maximizes if each nation specializes in goods in which it has a comparative advantage.

choices.label: A
choices.text: l only

choices.label: B
choices.text: II only

choices.label: C
choices.text: III only

choices.label: D
choices.text: II and III

questions.explanation: Statement I misdefines absolute advantage, which is the ability to produce more with the same resources; producing at lower opportunity cost is comparative advantage. Statements II and III are both correct, and III states the central result of trade theory.
questions.explanationJa: 記述Iは絶対優位の定義を誤っている。絶対優位とは同じ資源でより多く生産できることであり、より低い機会費用で生産できることは比較優位である。記述IIとIIIはいずれも正しく、IIIは貿易理論の中心的な結論を述べたものである。

questions.stem: Which of the following products are not complementary goods?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cars and tires

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chips and dip

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lamps and light bulbs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Video tapes and DVDs

questions.explanation: Complements are consumed together, so a rise in the price of one reduces demand for the other. Video tapes and DVDs are alternative ways of doing the same thing, which makes them substitutes: buyers move to one when the other becomes dearer.
questions.explanationJa: 補完財は一緒に消費されるので、一方の価格が上がれば他方の需要は減る。ビデオテープとDVDは同じ目的を果たす代替的な手段であり、したがって代替財である。一方が高くなれば買手はもう一方へ移る。

questions.stem: Tea and sugar cubes are complementary goods. Tea and coffee are substitute goods. What effect does a decrease in the price of tea have?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase the price of coffee

choices.label: B
choices.text: Shift the supply curve for sugar cubes to the left

choices.label: C
choices.text: Shift the demand curve for sugar cubes to the left

choices.label: D
choices.text: Shift the demand curve for sugar cubes to the right

questions.explanation: Cheaper tea means people drink more tea, and since sugar cubes go with it, more sugar is wanted at every sugar price: the demand curve for sugar shifts right. Nothing has changed in the cost of producing sugar, so its supply curve does not move.
questions.explanationJa: 紅茶が安くなれば人々はより多く紅茶を飲み、角砂糖はそれに伴って消費されるので、砂糖のどの価格水準でも需要量が増える。すなわち砂糖の需要曲線は右へシフトする。砂糖の生産コストには何の変化もないので、供給曲線は動かない。

questions.stem: What is the most likely result of increased safety regulations for bicycles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased bicycle prices

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increased bicycle consumption levels

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased bicycle prices

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased supply of bicycles

questions.explanation: Meeting stricter safety rules raises the cost of making each bicycle, so the supply curve shifts left. With demand unchanged, the new equilibrium is at a higher price and a lower quantity.
questions.explanationJa: より厳しい安全規制に適合させれば自転車1台当たりの製造コストが上がるので、供給曲線は左へシフトする。需要が変わらなければ、新しい均衡は価格が高く数量が少ないところに移る。

questions.stem: Over the past three years, widget manufacturing companies have established Internet sites for routine customer inquires about orders. Consequently, each customer service representative now handles five times as many customers. The costs of site maintenance are substantially less than one representative's wages. What is the most likely result of this change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lower wages for representatives

choices.label: B
choices.text: A widget supply curve shift to the left and increased widget prices

choices.label: C
choices.text: A widget supply curve shift to the left and decreased widget prices

choices.label: D
choices.text: A widget supply curve shift to the right and decreased widget prices

questions.explanation: Serving five times as many customers for less than one wage cuts the cost of supplying each widget, so the supply curve shifts right. Demand is unchanged, so the new equilibrium comes at a lower price and a higher quantity. The representatives' wages are set in the labour market, not by this efficiency gain.
questions.explanationJa: 1人分の賃金を下回る費用で5倍の顧客に対応できるようになれば、ウィジェット1個当たりの供給コストが下がるので、供給曲線は右へシフトする。需要は変わらないので、新しい均衡は価格が低く数量が多いところに移る。担当者の賃金は労働市場で決まるものであり、この効率化によって決まるわけではない。

questions.stem:
Essex Co. graphed the quantity supplied against price for its three products: E, F, and G. On the graph, price is on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal axis. Curve Se is the steepest, Sf is intermediate, and Sg is the flattest of the three.
Which product has the least price elasticity of supply?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Indeterminate from the given information

choices.label: B
choices.text: E

choices.label: C
choices.text: F

choices.label: D
choices.text: G

questions.explanation: The steeper the supply curve, the smaller the change in quantity for a given change in price, and therefore the lower the elasticity. Se is the steepest of the three, so product E has the least elastic supply. It is worth fixing this the right way round: steep means inelastic, flat means elastic.
questions.explanationJa: 供給曲線が急であるほど、同じ価格変化に対する数量の変化は小さく、したがって弾力性は低い。3本のうち最も急なのはSeなので、製品Eの供給が最も非弾力的である。方向を取り違えないよう押さえておきたい。急なら非弾力的、緩やかなら弾力的である。

questions.stem:
The total quantity of merle demanded changes when its price changes according to this schedule.
Quantity demanded | Unit price
1,500 units | $50
1,600 units | $40
1,700 units | $35
1,800 units | $32
Which is the price elasticity of demand for merle when the price decreases from $40 to $35?
questions.explanation: Elasticity = percentage change in quantity / percentage change in price, both measured from the starting point. Quantity: (1,700 - 1,600) / 1,600 = 6.25%. Price: ($35 - $40) / $40 = -12.5%. Elasticity = 6.25 / 12.5 = 0.5, so demand is inelastic over this range. Inverting the ratio gives 2.0, which is choice A.
questions.explanationJa: 弾力性 = 数量の変化率 ÷ 価格の変化率であり、いずれも起点を基準に測る。数量: (1,700 − 1,600) ÷ 1,600 = 6.25%。価格: ($35 − $40) ÷ $40 = −12.5%。弾力性 = 6.25 ÷ 12.5 = 0.5 となり、この範囲では需要は非弾力的である。比を逆にすると2.0となり、選択肢Aに落ちる。

questions.stem: What is the effect on the market price when both the supply and demand for a good increase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease only with inelastic demand

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease only with inelastic supply

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase only with inelastic demand

choices.label: D
choices.text: Indeterminate from the given information

questions.explanation: Rising demand pushes price up and rising supply pushes it down, so the outcome depends entirely on which shift is larger. Without that information the price effect cannot be signed, though quantity certainly rises.
questions.explanationJa: 需要の増加は価格を押し上げ、供給の増加は押し下げるので、結果はどちらのシフトが大きいかにすべて依存する。その情報がなければ価格への影響の符号は定められない。ただし数量が増えることは確実である。

questions.stem: What is the predictable effect when both the supply and demand for a good increase equally?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease both market-clearing quantity and price

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease market-clearing quantity only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decrease price only

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase market-clearing quantity only

questions.explanation: If the two shifts are of equal size, the upward pressure from demand and the downward pressure from supply cancel exactly, leaving price unchanged. Both shifts increase quantity, so the market-clearing quantity rises.
questions.explanationJa: 2つのシフトが同じ大きさであれば、需要側からの上向きの圧力と供給側からの下向きの圧力がちょうど相殺され、価格は変わらない。どちらのシフトも数量を増やすので、均衡数量は増加する。

questions.stem: Marginal utility

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreases when consumption expands

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increases when consumption expands

choices.label: C
choices.text: Indicates that a high consumption quantity is preferred to a low consumption quantity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Indicates that consumption decreases over time

questions.explanation: Marginal utility is the extra satisfaction from one more unit, and it falls as consumption expands: the first slice of pizza is worth more than the fifth. Total utility still rises, just by ever smaller amounts, until marginal utility reaches zero.
questions.explanationJa: 限界効用とは、もう1単位消費することから得られる追加の満足であり、消費が増えるにつれて低下する。ピザの1切れ目は5切れ目より価値が高い。総効用は依然として増えるが、その増え方が次第に小さくなり、やがて限界効用がゼロに達する。

questions.stem: What does the principle of diminishing marginal utility state?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Total utility declines as consumption of additional units of a specific product increases.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The price of a specific product decreases proportionately with its decrease in marginal utility.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Marginal utility declines when short-term supply curves are upward sloping.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Marginal utility declines as consumption of additional units of a specific product increases.

questions.explanation: The principle concerns the increment, not the total. Each additional unit adds less satisfaction than the one before, which is why the demand curve slopes downward: a buyer will pay less for a unit that is worth less. Choice A wrongly applies the decline to total utility.
questions.explanationJa: この原理が扱うのは増分であって総量ではない。追加の1単位が加える満足は、その前の1単位より小さい。需要曲線が右下がりになるのはこのためである。価値の小さい単位に対して買手は少ない金額しか払わない。選択肢Aは、この低下を総効用に当てはめてしまっている。

questions.stem: The net income presented on an income statement prepared in conforming with generally accepted accounting principles generally is

choices.label: A
choices.text: Equal to economic profit

choices.label: B
choices.text: Greater than economic profits because interest is not considered in calculating economic profits

choices.label: C
choices.text: Greater than economic profits because opportunity costs are not considered in calculating net income

choices.label: D
choices.text: Less than economic profits because economic profits don't include fixed costs

questions.explanation: Accounting net income deducts only explicit costs, the amounts actually paid. Economic profit also deducts implicit costs, the return the owner's own capital and labour could have earned elsewhere. Accounting income is therefore the larger of the two.
questions.explanationJa: 会計上の当期純利益は、実際に支払われた明示的費用だけを控除する。経済的利潤はこれに加えて、所有者自身の資本と労働が他の用途で得られたはずの報酬という暗黙的費用も控除する。したがって会計上の利益の方が大きくなる。

questions.stem: What is marginal revenue?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Equal to price in a monopoly market

choices.label: B
choices.text: The change in total revenue related to selling an additional unit

choices.label: C
choices.text: The change in total revenue related to increased prices

choices.label: D
choices.text: The change in cost associated with increasing returns of scale

questions.explanation: Marginal revenue is the change in total revenue from selling one more unit. In pure competition it equals price, since the extra unit sells without cutting the price; under monopoly it is below price, because selling more requires lowering the price on every unit.
questions.explanationJa: 限界収入とは、もう1単位販売することによる総収入の変化である。純粋競争のもとでは価格に等しい。追加の1単位は価格を下げずに売れるからである。独占のもとでは価格を下回る。より多く売るにはすべての単位について価格を下げなければならないためである。

questions.stem: Which of the following examples illustrates economies of scale?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Doubling the capacity of a day care facility requires compliance with more stringent regulations, resulting in more than double the costs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Each additional labor hour input to production is less efficient than the previous one.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increasing a factory's size results in lower average costs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increasing a factory’s size results in lower total costs.

questions.explanation: Economies of scale are about cost per unit, not cost in total: a larger factory that produces at a lower average cost is the definition. Choice D confuses the two, since total cost rises with output in any case; choice A describes diseconomies and choice B diminishing returns.
questions.explanationJa: 規模の経済は総額ではなく単位当たりのコストに関する概念であり、より大きな工場がより低い平均費用で生産することがその定義である。選択肢Dは両者を混同している。産出量が増えれば総費用はいずれにせよ増えるからである。選択肢Aは規模の不経済、選択肢Bは収穫逓減の説明である。

questions.stem: What is economic cost?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The opportunity cost less the explicit costs

choices.label: B
choices.text: The same as opportunity cost

choices.label: C
choices.text: The total of all explicit and implicit costs

choices.label: D
choices.text: The total revenue less total costs

questions.explanation: Economic cost covers everything the resources could have earned elsewhere: explicit costs actually paid plus implicit costs such as the owner's forgone salary and the return on the owner's capital. Choice D describes profit, not cost.
questions.explanationJa: 経済的費用は、その資源が他の用途で得られたはずのものをすべて含む。すなわち実際に支払われた明示的費用に、所有者が放棄した給与や所有者の資本に対する収益といった暗黙的費用を加えたものである。選択肢Dが述べているのは費用ではなく利潤である。

questions.stem: Cook Co.'s plant operates at 85% capacity. If inputs increase by one-sixth, additional output increases by one-twelfth. If inputs decrease by one-sixth, additional output decreases by one-twelfth. What best describes the relationship of Cook's average and marginal costs at 85% capacity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Average cost is equal to marginal cost

choices.label: B
choices.text: Average cost is greater than marginal cost

choices.label: C
choices.text: Average cost is less than marginal cost

choices.label: D
choices.text: The relationship is indeterminate with the given information

questions.explanation: Inputs rise by one-sixth but output by only one-twelfth, so each extra unit of output costs more than the average unit produced so far. Marginal cost therefore exceeds average cost, which is the region in which average cost is being pulled upward.
questions.explanationJa: 投入は6分の1増えるのに産出は12分の1しか増えないので、追加の産出1単位にかかる費用は、それまでに生産した平均的な1単位より高い。したがって限界費用は平均費用を上回っており、これは平均費用が押し上げられていく領域にあたる。

questions.stem: What is an example of a monopolistic competitive market?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lawn care service industry

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pharmaceutical industry

choices.label: C
choices.text: Restaurant industry

choices.label: D
choices.text: Wheat market

questions.explanation: Monopolistic competition combines many sellers and easy entry with differentiated products. Restaurants fit exactly: anyone can open one, but each offers a distinct menu, location, and atmosphere, so each has a little pricing power.
questions.explanationJa: 独占的競争は、多数の売手と容易な参入に、製品の差別化が組み合わさった市場である。レストランはまさにこれにあたる。誰でも開業できるが、それぞれ独自のメニュー・立地・雰囲気を持つので、各店が多少の価格決定力を持つ。

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best example of a purely competitive market?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Automobile industry

choices.label: B
choices.text: Lawn care service industry

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pharmaceutical industry

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ice cream industry

questions.explanation: Pure competition needs many small sellers offering an undifferentiated service with easy entry and exit. Lawn care comes closest: the service is essentially the same whoever performs it, and starting up requires little capital. Cars and pharmaceuticals are dominated by a few firms with heavily differentiated products.
questions.explanationJa: 純粋競争が成立するには、差別化されていないサービスを提供する多数の小規模な売手がいて、参入・退出が容易でなければならない。芝生の手入れがこれに最も近い。誰が行っても実質的に同じサービスであり、開業に必要な資本も少ない。自動車と医薬品は、高度に差別化された製品を持つ少数の企業が支配している。

questions.stem: Under what short-term circumstances will a manufacturer exit a market?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Price fall below average economic costs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Price fall below average fixed costs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Prices fall below average total costs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Prices fall below average variable costs.

questions.explanation: In the short run fixed costs are sunk and will be incurred whether or not the firm produces. So long as price covers average variable cost, operating contributes something toward those fixed costs. Once price falls below average variable cost, every unit sold deepens the loss, and shutting down is better.
questions.explanationJa: 短期では固定費は埋没しており、生産してもしなくても発生する。価格が平均変動費を賄っている限り、操業を続けることは固定費の一部を回収することに貢献する。価格が平均変動費を下回れば、1単位売るごとに損失が拡大するので、操業を停止する方がよい。

questions.stem: The labor market for masons is competitive and stable. What is the likely short-term result of an attempt to increase masons' wages?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased employment levels

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decreased employer size

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased employer size

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increased labor supplied

questions.explanation: A wage above the market-clearing level moves employers up their demand curve for labour, so fewer masons are hired, while more people want the work. The result is a surplus of labour, which is unemployment among masons.
questions.explanationJa: 市場の均衡水準を超える賃金は、雇用主を労働需要曲線に沿って上へ移動させるので、雇われる石工の数は減る一方、その仕事を望む人は増える。結果として労働の超過供給、すなわち石工の失業が生じる。

questions.stem: What is the classification of a market with low entry barriers, product differentiation, and many independent producers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Monopolistic competition

choices.label: B
choices.text: A monopoly

choices.label: C
choices.text: A natural monopoly

choices.label: D
choices.text: An oligopoly

questions.explanation: Many independent producers with easy entry rule out monopoly and oligopoly, while product differentiation rules out pure competition, which requires a homogeneous product. What is left is monopolistic competition.
questions.explanationJa: 多数の独立した生産者がいて参入が容易であることから独占と寡占は排除され、製品が差別化されていることから、同質の製品を前提とする純粋競争も排除される。残るのが独占的競争である。

questions.stem: What is not characteristic of perfect competition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Few entry or exit barriers

choices.label: B
choices.text: High customer loyalty

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many independent producers

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perfect information

questions.explanation: Perfect competition assumes a homogeneous product, so buyers have no reason to prefer one seller over another and switch freely on price alone. Customer loyalty would give a seller pricing power, which the model rules out by construction.
questions.explanationJa: 完全競争は同質の製品を前提とするので、買手にはある売手を他より選ぶ理由がなく、価格だけを見て自由に乗り換える。顧客の忠誠心は売手に価格決定力を与えることになり、このモデルは構造上それを排除している。

questions.stem: What does a high concentration ratio indicate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Monopolistic competition

choices.label: B
choices.text: A monopoly

choices.label: C
choices.text: An oligopoly

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pure competition

questions.explanation: The concentration ratio is the share of industry sales held by the largest few firms. A high ratio means a handful of firms account for most of the market, which is the definition of an oligopoly. A monopoly would be a single firm, essentially a ratio of 100% for one seller.
questions.explanationJa: 集中度指標（concentration ratio）は、上位数社が業界の売上に占める割合である。この比率が高いことは、ごく少数の企業が市場の大半を占めていることを意味し、これが寡占の定義である。独占であれば企業は1社であり、実質的に1社で100%となる。

questions.stem: Neal City requires taxicabs to display a medallion. Neal issued a limited number of these medallions; those wishing to become taxi operators must purchase medallions from current holders, although no one may own more than 30% of the medallions. Taxi fares must be in accordance with a maximum price schedule set by the city; no medallion holder sets fares lower than the municipal schedule. To taxi operators, what term best describes these medallions?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cartel

choices.label: B
choices.text: Collusion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Entry barrier

choices.label: D
choices.text: Exit barrier

questions.explanation: The medallion is the price of admission: no one can operate without buying one from an existing holder, and the city limits how many exist. That is an entry barrier. A cartel or collusion would require the operators themselves to agree on price, whereas here the city sets the schedule.
questions.explanationJa: メダリオンは市場に入るための対価である。既存の保有者から買わなければ営業できず、その総数は市が制限している。これが参入障壁である。カルテルや談合であれば営業者同士が価格を取り決めることになるが、ここで料金表を定めているのは市である。

questions.stem: The marginal cost curve is the supply curve for a business in what type of market?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Monopolistic competition

choices.label: B
choices.text: A monopoly

choices.label: C
choices.text: A natural monopoly

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pure competition

questions.explanation: A purely competitive firm takes the price as given, so it produces up to the point where marginal cost equals that price. Reading off how much it will supply at each price therefore traces its marginal cost curve above average variable cost. A firm with pricing power chooses quantity where marginal cost equals marginal revenue, not price, so no such supply curve exists.
questions.explanationJa: 純粋競争のもとでの企業は価格を与えられたものとして受け取るので、限界費用がその価格と等しくなる点まで生産する。したがって各価格でいくら供給するかをたどると、平均変動費を上回る範囲の限界費用曲線そのものになる。価格決定力を持つ企業は、価格ではなく限界収入と限界費用が等しくなる数量を選ぶので、このような供給曲線は存在しない。

questions.stem: What volume provides the most profitable results for companies in monopolist and monopolist competitive markets?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Where average costs are minimized

choices.label: B
choices.text: Where marginal costs equals marginal revenue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Where price equals marginal cost

choices.label: D
choices.text: Where price equals average cost

questions.explanation: Profit is maximized where marginal cost equals marginal revenue, and this holds in every market structure. What differs is that a firm with pricing power faces a marginal revenue below its price, so it stops short of the output where price equals marginal cost.
questions.explanationJa: 利潤が最大になるのは限界費用と限界収入が等しくなる点であり、これはどの市場構造でも成り立つ。異なるのは、価格決定力を持つ企業では限界収入が価格を下回るため、価格と限界費用が一致する産出量には達しないところで生産を止める点である。

questions.stem: What is the effect of economic profit in a pure monopoly market?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease in the number of producers

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease in prices for substitutes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase in the number of producers

choices.label: D
choices.text: No influence on the number of producers

questions.explanation: In pure competition, economic profit attracts entrants until it is competed away. A pure monopoly is defined by barriers that prevent entry, so the profit persists and the number of producers stays at one.
questions.explanationJa: 純粋競争では、経済的利潤が新規参入を招き、やがて競争によって消える。純粋独占は参入を妨げる障壁によって定義されるので、利潤は持続し、生産者の数は1社のまま変わらない。

questions.stem: What is disposable income?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The sum of consumption spending, interest payments, and savings

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gross domestic product divided by population, adjusted for inflation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Net domestic product plus a country's net income earned abroad less indirect business taxes

choices.label: D
choices.text: The total market value of all final goods and service produced within a specified country, less depreciation

questions.explanation: Disposable income is what households have left after taxes, and it can only be spent, paid out as interest, or saved. The other three describe per capita GDP, national income, and net domestic product.
questions.explanationJa: 可処分所得とは、家計に税引後に残る所得であり、その使い道は消費・利払い・貯蓄のいずれかしかない。他の3つは1人当たりGDP、国民所得、国内純生産の説明である。

questions.stem: Variations between business cycles most likely are attributable to which of the following factors?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The law of diminishing returns

choices.label: B
choices.text: Comparative advantage

choices.label: C
choices.text: Duration and intensity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Opportunity costs

questions.explanation: Every cycle runs through the same four phases, so what distinguishes one from another is how long each phase lasts and how far output swings. That is duration and intensity; the other three are microeconomic concepts unrelated to cyclical variation.
questions.explanationJa: 景気循環はいずれも同じ4つの局面をたどるので、循環同士を分けるのは各局面がどれだけ続き、産出量がどれだけ振れるかである。すなわち期間と振幅である。他の3つは景気変動とは無関係なミクロ経済の概念である。

questions.stem: What is characteristic of the recession of a business cycle?

choices.label: A
choices.text: low unemployment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excessive productive capacity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increasing capital investments

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increasing price levels

questions.explanation: In a recession demand falls short of what the economy can produce, so plant stands idle and capacity is excessive relative to output. Unemployment rises rather than falls, firms postpone investment, and price pressure eases.
questions.explanationJa: 景気後退では、需要が経済の生産能力に届かないので設備が遊休し、産出量に比べて能力が過剰になる。失業は減るのではなく増え、企業は投資を先送りし、物価上昇の圧力は和らぐ。

questions.stem: What action would the Federal Reserve most likely take to implement an expansionary monetary policy?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease the discount rate and increase the reserve requirement

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease the discount rate and purchase U.S. government debt securities

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the discount rate and decrease the reserve requirement

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the discount rate and sell U.S. government debt securities

questions.explanation: Expansion means adding reserves and making credit cheaper. Buying government securities pays cash into the banking system, and a lower discount rate reduces the cost of borrowing from the Fed. The other choices pair an expansionary step with a contractionary one, or are contractionary throughout.
questions.explanationJa: 金融緩和とは、準備預金を増やし信用を安くすることである。国債の買入れは銀行システムに現金を供給し、公定歩合の引き下げは連邦準備銀行からの借入コストを下げる。他の選択肢は緩和策と引き締め策を組み合わせているか、全体が引き締め策である。

questions.stem: What is characteristic of a business cycle trough?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreasing purchasing power

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increasing capital investments

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rising costs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Unused productive capacity

questions.explanation: The trough is the bottom of the cycle: demand is at its weakest, so plant and labour sit idle. Rising costs and increasing investment belong to the expansion, and purchasing power is not falling because inflationary pressure is absent.
questions.explanationJa: 谷（trough）は循環の底であり、需要が最も弱いので設備も労働も遊休する。コストの上昇や投資の増加は拡張局面の特徴であり、インフレ圧力がないので購買力が低下することもない。

questions.stem: What condition exists when the addition of capital goods exceeds the capital consumption allowance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Equilibrium investment

choices.label: B
choices.text: Negative gross investment

choices.label: C
choices.text: Negative net investment

choices.label: D
choices.text: Positive net investment

questions.explanation: Gross investment is all new capital goods; the capital consumption allowance is the depreciation of the existing stock. When new additions exceed that wear and tear, net investment is positive and the capital stock grows.
questions.explanationJa: 総投資は新たに追加される資本財の全体であり、資本減耗引当（capital consumption allowance）は既存ストックの減耗分である。新規の追加がこの減耗を上回れば純投資はプラスとなり、資本ストックは増加する。

questions.stem: Which of the following are not assumptions of the supply-side theory of economics?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cuts in taxes will produce a recovery due to an increase in aggregate demand and increased motivation for investment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Excessive monetary growth leads to inflation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased income would result in the same aggregate tax revenues despite lower tax rates, so spending cuts are not needed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A progressive tax structure is a disincentive to increased investment.

questions.explanation: Supply-side economics argues that lower marginal tax rates spur work, saving, and investment, that a progressive structure discourages investment, and that the resulting growth can hold tax revenue up. The claim that excessive monetary growth causes inflation is monetarism, a separate school.
questions.explanationJa: サプライサイド経済学は、限界税率の引き下げが労働・貯蓄・投資を促すこと、累進的な税構造が投資を阻害すること、そして結果として生じる成長が税収を維持しうることを主張する。過剰な通貨供給がインフレを招くという主張はマネタリズムであり、別の学派に属する。

questions.stem: The federal government measures inflation with which of the following indicators?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dow Jones index

choices.label: B
choices.text: Consumer price index

choices.label: C
choices.text: Consumer confidence index

choices.label: D
choices.text: Corporate profits

questions.explanation: The consumer price index tracks the cost of a fixed basket of household purchases, and its change over time is the standard measure of inflation. The Dow measures share prices, consumer confidence measures sentiment, and corporate profits measure business results.
questions.explanationJa: 消費者物価指数は、家計が購入する一定のバスケットの費用を追跡するものであり、その時系列の変化がインフレの標準的な尺度となる。ダウ平均は株価、消費者信頼感指数は心理、企業利益は事業成績を測る指標である。

questions.stem: The primary purpose of the consumer price index (CPI) is to

choices.label: A
choices.text: Establish a cost-of-living index

choices.label: B
choices.text: Identify the strength of an economic recovery

choices.label: C
choices.text: Help determine the Federal Reserve Bank’s discount rate

choices.label: D
choices.text: Compare relative price changes over time

questions.explanation: The CPI exists to measure how prices move over time, by pricing the same basket period after period. It is often used as a cost-of-living proxy, but it is not one: it holds the basket fixed and so ignores the substitution consumers make when relative prices change.
questions.explanationJa: CPIは、同じバスケットを期間ごとに評価することで、物価が時系列でどう動くかを測るために存在する。生活費指数の代用として使われることが多いが、それそのものではない。バスケットを固定するため、相対価格の変化に応じて消費者が行う代替を捉えられないからである。

questions.stem: What is characteristic of a period of rising inflation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increases the purchasing power of money

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increases the price level and decreases the purchasing power of money

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increases the price level, which benefits anyone who is owed a specific amount of money

choices.label: D
choices.text: Benefits anyone who is owed a specific amount of money and harms anyone who owes a specific amount

questions.explanation: Inflation is a rise in the general price level, which is the same thing as a fall in what a unit of money will buy. It transfers value from creditors, who are repaid in weaker dollars, to debtors, so choices C and D have the direction reversed.
questions.explanationJa: インフレとは一般物価水準の上昇であり、それは貨幣1単位で買えるものが減ることと同義である。価値は債権者から債務者へ移転する。債権者は価値の目減りしたドルで返済を受けるからである。したがって選択肢CとDは向きが逆である。

questions.stem: Which of the following economic terms describes a general decline in prices for goods and services and in the level of interest rates?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Expansion

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inflation

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deflation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recession

questions.explanation: Deflation is a sustained fall in the general price level, and it typically comes with weak demand, which also pulls nominal interest rates down. Recession describes falling output rather than falling prices, though the two often occur together.
questions.explanationJa: デフレーションとは一般物価水準の持続的な下落であり、通常は需要の弱さを伴い、それが名目金利も押し下げる。リセッションは物価ではなく産出量の減少を指す概念であり、両者はしばしば同時に起こるが同じものではない。

questions.stem: What is an example of indirect taxes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Social Security taxes paid by employees

choices.label: B
choices.text: Real property taxes paid by landlords

choices.label: C
choices.text: Real property taxes paid by homeowners

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intangible property taxes paid by businesses

questions.explanation: An indirect tax is one the payer can pass on to someone else. A landlord builds property tax into the rent, so tenants ultimately bear it. A homeowner has no one to pass it to, and taxes on employees and on a business's own property are borne directly.
questions.explanationJa: 間接税とは、納税者が他者へ転嫁できる税である。家主は固定資産税を家賃に織り込むので、最終的には借家人が負担する。持ち家所有者には転嫁する相手がおらず、従業員が負担する税や事業者自身の資産に対する税は直接に負担される。

questions.stem: What is the most likely impact of government transfer payments?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease aggregate demand for goods provided by the private sector

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase aggregate demand for goods provided by the private sector

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase aggregate demand for goods provided by the public sector

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reallocate the consumption of goods within the private sector

questions.explanation: A transfer payment moves purchasing power from taxpayers to recipients without the government buying anything itself. Total private spending is broadly unchanged; what changes is who does the spending and therefore which goods are bought.
questions.explanationJa: 移転支出は、政府自身が何かを購入することなく、購買力を納税者から受給者へ移すものである。民間支出の総額はおおむね変わらず、変わるのは誰が支出するか、したがってどの財が買われるかである。

questions.stem:
Based on the following assumptions of the production potential of one unit of resources:
Beef | Chips
Argentina | 15 tons | 1,800 units
Taiwan | 6 tons | 1,500 units
In trade between Argentina and Taiwan, Taiwan has

choices.label: A
choices.text: An absolute advantage in producing beef

choices.label: B
choices.text: An absolute advantage in producing chips

choices.label: C
choices.text: A comparative advantage in producing beef

choices.label: D
choices.text: A comparative advantage in producing chips

questions.explanation: Comparative advantage is about opportunity cost. For Argentina one ton of beef costs 1,800 / 15 = 120 chips; for Taiwan it costs 1,500 / 6 = 250. Taiwan gives up more chips per ton of beef, so it should make chips, and Argentina beef. Argentina has the absolute advantage in both, which is why the answer turns on opportunity cost rather than output.
questions.explanationJa: 比較優位は機会費用の問題である。アルゼンチンでは牛肉1トンの機会費用が 1,800 ÷ 15 = 120チップ、台湾では 1,500 ÷ 6 = 250チップである。台湾の方が牛肉1トンのために犠牲にするチップが多いので、台湾はチップを、アルゼンチンは牛肉を生産すべきことになる。絶対優位はアルゼンチンが両財で持っており、だからこそ判断の根拠が産出量ではなく機会費用になる。

questions.stem:
Based on the following assumptions of the production potential of one unit of resources:
Beef | Chips
Argentina | 15 tons | 1,800 units
Taiwan | 6 tons | 1,500 units
If free trade exists between Argentina and Taiwan,

choices.label: A
choices.text: Argentina would export chips to Taiwan.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Argentina would specialize in both chip and beef production.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Taiwan would not gain any advantage from Argentina imports.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taiwan would specialize in chip production.

questions.explanation: Each country specializes where its opportunity cost is lower, so Taiwan makes chips and Argentina beef, and they trade. Even though Argentina could produce more of both, specializing frees its resources for the good it gives up least to make, and both countries end up with more than they could produce alone.
questions.explanationJa: 各国は機会費用の低い財に特化するので、台湾はチップを、アルゼンチンは牛肉を生産して交易する。アルゼンチンは両方をより多く生産できるが、特化することで、最も少ない犠牲で作れる財へ資源を集中できる。その結果、両国とも単独で生産できる量を上回るものを手にする。

questions.stem:
Based on the following assumptions of the production potential of one unit of resources:
Beef | Chips
Argentina | 15 tons | 1,800 units
Taiwan | 6 tons | 1,500 units
If free trade exists between Argentina and Taiwan, the relative price of beef and chips would be

choices.label: A
choices.text: Exactly 120 chips for one ton of beef.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exactly 250 chips for one ton of beef.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Within 0.008 and 0.009 tons of beef for one chip.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Within 120 and 250 chips for one ton of beef.

questions.explanation: Trade only benefits both sides if the exchange rate sits between the two domestic opportunity costs. Argentina will not accept fewer than 120 chips per ton, since it can make 120 itself; Taiwan will not pay more than 250, for the same reason. The terms therefore fall between 120 and 250.
questions.explanationJa: 貿易が双方の利益になるのは、交換比率が両国の国内機会費用の間に収まる場合だけである。アルゼンチンは自国で120チップを作れるので、牛肉1トンにつき120未満では応じない。台湾も同じ理由で250を超えては払わない。したがって交易条件は120と250の間に落ち着く。

questions.stem: Ice skates and skis are substitute goods. What causes the demand curve for ice skates to shift to the right?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A decrease in average household income

choices.label: B
choices.text: A decrease in the popularity of skating

choices.label: C
choices.text: A decrease in the price of ski equipment

choices.label: D
choices.text: An increase in the population

questions.explanation: A rightward shift means more is wanted at every price, and a larger population adds buyers. A fall in the price of skis would send buyers to skis and shift skate demand left; lower income and reduced popularity also shift it left.
questions.explanationJa: 右へのシフトとは、あらゆる価格でより多く需要されることを意味し、人口の増加は買手を増やす。スキー用品の値下がりは買手をスキーへ向かわせ、スケート靴の需要曲線を左へシフトさせる。所得の減少や人気の低下も同様に左へシフトさせる。

questions.stem: What does a supply curve illustrate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The relationship between costs and quantity supplied

choices.label: B
choices.text: The relationship between demand and supply

choices.label: C
choices.text: The relationship between income and price

choices.label: D
choices.text: The relationship between price and quantity supplied

questions.explanation: A supply curve shows how much sellers will offer at each price, holding everything else constant. Costs and other determinants are what shift the whole curve; they are not the axes of it.
questions.explanationJa: 供給曲線は、他の条件を一定としたときに、各価格で売手がどれだけ供給するかを示す。コストなどの決定要因は曲線全体をシフトさせるものであって、曲線の軸ではない。

questions.stem: Under what circumstances is the complete purchase price of natural resources deemed economic rent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Completely Elastic supply

choices.label: B
choices.text: Fixed and limited supply

choices.label: C
choices.text: Legislated celling price

choices.label: D
choices.text: Legislated floor price

questions.explanation: Economic rent is payment above the minimum needed to bring a resource into use. When supply is completely fixed, as with land or a mineral deposit, the quantity is there regardless of price, so no part of the payment is needed to call it forth and the entire price is rent.
