questions.explanationJa: 経済的レントとは、ある資源を用途に供させるために必要な最低額を超える支払である。土地や鉱床のように供給が完全に固定されている場合、価格がいくらであろうとその数量は存在するので、供給を引き出すために必要な部分は存在せず、支払額の全額がレントとなる。

questions.stem: Noodles have a 0.7 price elasticity of demand. What is the best description of the state of demand for noodles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Elastic

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inelastic

choices.label: C
choices.text: Perfectly elastic

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perfectly inelastic

questions.explanation: Elasticity below 1 means quantity responds proportionally less than price, which is inelastic demand. At 0.7, a 10% price rise cuts quantity by only 7%, so total revenue rises. Perfectly elastic and perfectly inelastic are the limiting cases of infinity and zero.
questions.explanationJa: 弾力性が1を下回るとは、数量の反応が価格の変化に比べて比例的に小さいこと、すなわち非弾力的な需要を意味する。0.7であれば、価格が10%上がっても数量は7%しか減らないので、総収入は増加する。完全弾力的と完全非弾力的は、それぞれ無限大とゼロという極限の場合である。

questions.stem: When does demand for a product tend to be price inelastic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consumers spend a large proportion of income on the product.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Few good complements to the product exist.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Few good substitutes for the product exist.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The product is a luxury item.

questions.explanation: Demand is inelastic when buyers have nowhere to turn, so the absence of close substitutes is the key condition. A luxury and a product taking a large share of income both invite a strong response to price, and complements affect the level of demand rather than its sensitivity.
questions.explanationJa: 需要が非弾力的になるのは、買手に他に行き場がないときなので、近い代替財が存在しないことが決定的な条件である。贅沢品であることや所得に占める割合が大きいことは、いずれも価格への反応を強める。補完財は需要の水準に影響するのであって、価格感応度を左右するものではない。

questions.stem: Broccoli and peas are substitutes. What is the most likely effect of an increase in the market supply of broccoli?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease in the quantity of broccoli demanded

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease in the price of broccoli

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase in the quantity of peas demanded

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase in the price of peas

questions.explanation: A larger supply of broccoli shifts its supply curve right, so the price of broccoli falls. Since peas are substitutes, cheaper broccoli draws buyers away from peas, reducing demand for peas and pushing their price down, so choices C and D are backwards.
questions.explanationJa: ブロッコリーの供給が増えれば供給曲線は右へシフトし、ブロッコリーの価格は下がる。えんどう豆は代替財なので、安くなったブロッコリーが買手を引き寄せ、えんどう豆の需要は減って価格も下がる。したがって選択肢CとDは逆である。

questions.stem: In competitive markets, what generally is the short-term result of a government price celling set below the equilibrium market price?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased demand

choices.label: B
choices.text: No effect

choices.label: C
choices.text: Shortage

choices.label: D
choices.text: Surplus

questions.explanation: A ceiling below equilibrium holds the price where buyers want more than sellers will provide, and the price is not allowed to rise to close the gap. The excess of quantity demanded over quantity supplied is a shortage. A ceiling above equilibrium would simply not bind.
questions.explanationJa: 均衡を下回る上限価格は、買手が求める量が売手の供給量を上回る水準に価格を固定し、その差を埋めるところまで価格が上がることを許さない。需要量が供給量を超える状態が不足である。均衡を上回る上限価格であれば、そもそも拘束力を持たない。

questions.stem:
Based on the following daily information about Dane Company.
Number of | Total Units | Average
Employees | Produced | Selling Price
100 | 2,000 | $50
101 | 2,030 | $46
102 | 2,080 | $45
What is Dane's marginal revenue per unit when the 102nd additional employee is added?
questions.explanation: Total revenue = units x price: 101 employees give 2,030 x $46 = $93,380 and 102 give 2,080 x $45 = $93,600. Revenue rises $220 while output rises 50 units, so marginal revenue per unit = $220 / 50 = $4.40. It is far below the $45 selling price because adding output forced the price down on every unit sold.
questions.explanationJa: 総収入 = 数量 × 価格。従業員101人では 2,030 × $46 = $93,380、102人では 2,080 × $45 = $93,600。収入は $220 増え、産出は50単位増えるので、単位当たり限界収入 = $220 ÷ 50 = $4.40。販売価格 $45 を大きく下回るのは、産出を増やしたことで販売する全単位について価格が下がったためである。

questions.stem:
Based on the following daily information about Dane Company.
Number of | Total Units | Average
Employees | Produced | Selling Price
100 | 2,000 | $50
101 | 2,030 | $46
102 | 2,080 | $45
What is Dane's marginal revenue product when the 102nd additional employee is added?
questions.explanation: The marginal revenue product is the extra revenue the additional worker brings in, that is, the whole change in total revenue: $93,600 - $93,380 = $220. It is what the firm can afford to pay that worker, and it differs from marginal revenue per unit, which spreads the same $220 over the 50 extra units.
questions.explanationJa: 限界収入生産物とは、追加した1人の労働者がもたらす収入の増加分、すなわち総収入の変化額そのものである: $93,600 − $93,380 = $220。これがその労働者に支払いうる上限であり、同じ $220 を追加の50単位に割り振った単位当たり限界収入とは別の概念である。

questions.stem:
Based on the following daily information about Dane Company.
Number of | Total Units | Average
Employees | Produced | Selling Price
100 | 2,000 | $50
101 | 2,030 | $46
102 | 2,080 | $45
What is Dane's marginal physical product when the 101st additional employee is added?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 30 units

choices.label: B
choices.text: 50 units

choices.label: C
choices.text: 2,000 units

choices.label: D
choices.text: 2,030 units

questions.explanation: Marginal physical product is the extra output from one more worker, measured in units: 2,030 - 2,000 = 30 units. Note that the 102nd worker adds 50 units, more than the 101st, so diminishing returns have not yet set in over this range.
questions.explanationJa: 限界物的生産物とは、労働者を1人増やしたことによる産出の増加分を数量で測ったものである: 2,030 − 2,000 = 30単位。なお102人目は50単位を加えており101人目を上回るので、この範囲ではまだ収穫逓減は始まっていない。

questions.stem: Which of the following is characteristic of a perfectly competitive market?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consumers avoid diminishing returns.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Consumers exhibit high brand loyalty.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Consumers purchase goods at the lowest price.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Producers often will produce goods at below average cost due to high exit barriers

questions.explanation: With a homogeneous product and full information, buyers have no reason to pay more than the lowest price on offer, and any seller charging more sells nothing. Brand loyalty and exit barriers belong to other market structures, and diminishing returns is a production concept, not a consumer one.
questions.explanationJa: 製品が同質で情報が完全であれば、買手には提示されている最安値を超えて支払う理由がなく、それより高い価格を付ける売手は1つも売れない。ブランドへの忠誠心や退出障壁は他の市場構造の特徴であり、収穫逓減は消費者ではなく生産に関する概念である。

questions.stem: Which of following is characteristic of an oligopoly market?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mutual influence among industry firms on each other’s prices

choices.label: B
choices.text: No entry or exit barriers

choices.label: C
choices.text: No promotional or informational advertising

choices.label: D
choices.text: One seller of a product with no close substitutes

questions.explanation: An oligopoly has so few sellers that each must consider how the others will react before changing price, which is what makes the kinked demand curve and price leadership arise. Choice D describes a monopoly, and the other two contradict the heavy advertising and entry barriers oligopolies typically show.
questions.explanationJa: 寡占では売手が非常に少ないため、各社は価格を変える前に他社がどう反応するかを考慮しなければならない。屈折需要曲線やプライスリーダーシップが生じるのはこのためである。選択肢Dは独占の説明であり、他の2つは寡占が通常示す活発な広告と参入障壁に反する。

questions.stem: What is the classification of a market with homogeneous products, few entry or exit barriers, many independent producers, and low customer loyalty?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Monopolistic competition

choices.label: B
choices.text: A monopoly

choices.label: C
choices.text: A natural monopoly

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pure competition

questions.explanation: Homogeneous products with low loyalty, many producers, and free entry are precisely the assumptions of pure competition. Monopolistic competition would require differentiated products, and the two monopoly forms require a single seller.
questions.explanationJa: 同質の製品で顧客の固定化がなく、生産者が多数で参入が自由であることは、まさに純粋競争の前提である。独占的競争であれば製品の差別化が必要であり、2つの独占形態はいずれも売手が1社であることを要する。

questions.stem:
Based on the following information about Tamar, a nation with a population of 100,000. Tamar had the following financial transactions for the year.
Gross domestic product | £5,000,000
Transfer payments | 625,000
Corporate income taxes | 60,000
National retirement plan contributions | 250,000
National retirement plan disbursements | 220,000
Indirect business taxes | 210,000
Personal taxes | 300,000
Undistributed corporate profits | 25,000
Depreciation | 600,000
Net income earned abroad | 50,000
What is Tamar's net domestic product?
questions.explanation: Net domestic product = GDP - depreciation = £5,000,000 - £600,000 = £4,400,000. Depreciation, or the capital consumption allowance, is deducted because that much output merely replaced capital used up, so it did not add to the nation's wealth.
questions.explanationJa: 国内純生産 = GDP − 減価償却 = £5,000,000 − £600,000 = £4,400,000。減価償却（資本減耗引当）を控除するのは、その分の産出が消耗した資本の置き換えにすぎず、国の富を増やしていないからである。

questions.stem:
Based on the following information about Tamar, a nation with a population of 100,000. Tamar had the following financial transactions for the year.
Gross domestic product | £5,000,000
Transfer payments | 625,000
Corporate income taxes | 60,000
National retirement plan contributions | 250,000
National retirement plan disbursements | 220,000
Indirect business taxes | 210,000
Personal taxes | 300,000
Undistributed corporate profits | 25,000
Depreciation | 600,000
Net income earned abroad | 50,000
What is Tamar's national income?
questions.explanation: National income measures what the nation's own factors earned, so start from net domestic product, add the net income its residents earned abroad, and remove indirect business taxes, which are part of the price but not income to any factor: £4,400,000 + £50,000 - £210,000 = £4,240,000.
questions.explanationJa: 国民所得は、その国の生産要素が稼いだ額を測るものなので、国内純生産から出発し、居住者が海外で得た純所得を加え、価格の一部ではあるがどの生産要素の所得にもならない間接税を差し引く: £4,400,000 + £50,000 − £210,000 = £4,240,000。

Based on the following information about Tamar, a nation with a population of 100,000. Tamar had the following financial transactions for the year.
Gross domestic product | £5,000,000
Transfer payments | 625,000
Corporate income taxes | 60,000
National retirement plan contributions | 250,000
National retirement plan disbursements | 220,000
Indirect business taxes | 210,000
Personal taxes | 300,000
Undistributed corporate profits | 25,000
Depreciation | 600,000
Net income earned abroad | 50,000
What is Tamar's personal income?
questions.explanation: Personal income is what households actually receive, so remove the earnings that never reach them and add the receipts that do not arise from production: £4,240,000 - £60,000 corporate income taxes - £25,000 undistributed profits + £625,000 transfer payments = £4,780,000. Note that under the fuller national accounts definition social insurance contributions are also deducted; this question's answer set does not do so, so the retirement plan figures are left aside.
questions.explanationJa: 個人所得は家計が実際に受け取る額なので、家計に届かない稼得を除き、生産から生じたのではない受取を加える: £4,240,000 − 法人所得税 £60,000 − 内部留保 £25,000 + 移転支出 £625,000 = £4,780,000。なお国民経済計算のより厳密な定義では社会保険拠出も控除されるが、この設問の選択肢はそれを行っていないので、退職年金制度の数値は使わない。

What is Tamar's real per-capita output?
questions.explanation: Per capita output divides total output by the population: £5,000,000 / 100,000 = £50.00. Since the figures are for a single year, no price adjustment is needed; the real and nominal figures coincide when the year in question is the base year.
questions.explanationJa: 1人当たり産出は総産出を人口で割ったものである: £5,000,000 ÷ 100,000 = £50.00。単年度の数値なので物価調整は不要である。対象年が基準年である場合、実質値と名目値は一致する。

questions.stem: Which of the following concepts compares the price of goods in a given year to a base year?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consumer price index

choices.label: B
choices.text: Consumer confidence index

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gross national product

choices.label: D
choices.text: Net national product

questions.explanation: The consumer price index prices the same basket of goods each period and expresses the result relative to a base year set at 100, so the index directly measures how prices have moved since that year. GNP and NNP measure output, not prices.
questions.explanationJa: 消費者物価指数は、毎期同じバスケットの財を評価し、その結果を100とした基準年に対する相対値で表すので、基準年以降に物価がどう動いたかを直接に測る。GNPやNNPが測るのは物価ではなく産出量である。

questions.stem: If a law establishes a maximum price for product Y in a competitive market and the ceiling price is above the market or equilibrium price for product Y,

choices.label: A
choices.text: The law has no effect on the market of good Y.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A surplus of good Y will occur.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Supply of Y will decrease as price increases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A shortage for Y will occur.

questions.explanation: A price ceiling only binds if it sits below the equilibrium price. Set above it, the market clears at the lower equilibrium price on its own and the ceiling is never reached, so nothing changes. A shortage would need a ceiling below equilibrium, and a surplus needs a floor above it.
questions.explanationJa: 上限価格が拘束力を持つのは、均衡価格を下回る水準に設定された場合だけである。均衡より上に置かれれば、市場は自力でそれより低い均衡価格で取引され、上限に触れることがないので何も変わらない。不足が生じるには均衡を下回る上限価格が、余剰が生じるには均衡を上回る下限価格が必要である。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.1 (code 9911)

questions.stem: If the demand for cigars in Miami is relatively elastic, and Miami imposes high taxes on cigars that result in higher cigar prices, then in Miami

choices.label: A
choices.text: The quantity of cigars demanded would increase.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The demand for cigars would increase.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The demand curve for cigars would become vertical.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Expenditures on cigars would fall.

questions.explanation: Expenditure is price times quantity. When demand is elastic the quantity falls proportionally more than the price rises, so the product of the two shrinks and total spending on cigars falls. Quantity demanded goes down rather than up, and a tax does not move the demand curve or change its shape.
questions.explanationJa: 支出額は価格と数量の積である。需要が弾力的な場合、価格の上昇率より数量の減少率の方が大きいので、両者の積は縮み、葉巻への支出総額は減る。需要量は増えるのではなく減り、課税は需要曲線を移動させることも形を変えることもない。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.2 (code 9911)

questions.stem: If the coefficient of elasticity is two, then the consumer demand for the product is said to be

choices.label: A
choices.text: Unit elastic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Elastic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inelastic.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Perfectly inelastic.

questions.explanation: Elasticity above 1 means quantity responds proportionally more than price, which is elastic demand. A coefficient of 2 says a 1% price change moves quantity 2%. Unit elastic is exactly 1, inelastic is below 1, and perfectly inelastic is zero.
questions.explanationJa: 弾力性が1を超えることは、数量が価格より比例的に大きく反応すること、すなわち弾力的な需要を意味する。係数2は、価格が1%変化すると数量が2%動くということである。単位弾力的はちょうど1、非弾力的は1未満、完全非弾力的はゼロである。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.3 (code 7211)

questions.stem: If the average household income decreases and there is no change in the price of a normal good, then the

choices.label: A
choices.text: Supply curve will shift to the right.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Quantity demanded will move farther up the demand curve.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Demand will shift to the right.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Demand curve will shift to the left.

questions.explanation: For a normal good, less income means less is wanted at every price, so the whole demand curve shifts left. A movement along the curve would require the good's own price to change, and here the price is stated to be unchanged.
questions.explanationJa: 通常財では、所得が減ればあらゆる価格で需要量が減るので、需要曲線全体が左へシフトする。曲線上の移動が起きるにはその財自身の価格が変わる必要があるが、ここでは価格は変わらないと明示されている。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.4 (code 9911)

questions.stem: An increase in the price of a complementary good will

choices.label: A
choices.text: Shift the demand curve of the joint commodity to the right.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease the price paid for a substitute good.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Shift the supply curve of the joint commodity to the right.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Shift the demand curve of the joint commodity to the left.

questions.explanation: Complements are consumed together, so making one dearer reduces the quantity of the pair that people buy. Less of the joint commodity is wanted at every price, which is a leftward shift of its demand curve. Its production costs are untouched, so supply does not move.
questions.explanationJa: 補完財は一緒に消費されるので、一方が高くなればその組合せ自体の購入量が減る。相手方の財はあらゆる価格で需要量が減り、これは需要曲線の左シフトにあたる。生産コストには影響がないので供給曲線は動かない。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.5 (code 9911)

questions.stem: If shoes are part of the consumers’ basket of goods, and the Consumer Price lndex increased by 6% for the year while the price of shoes increased by 2%, then

choices.label: A
choices.text: The supply curve will shift to the left.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Neither the demand curve nor the supply curve will be affected.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The demand curve will shift to the right.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The demand curve will shift to the left.

questions.explanation: Prices in general rose 6% while shoes rose only 2%, so shoes became cheaper relative to everything else even though their money price went up. Buyers substitute toward the relatively cheaper good, and demand for shoes shifts right.
questions.explanationJa: 物価全体が6%上昇したのに対し靴は2%しか上がっていないので、名目価格は上がっていても、他のすべてに比べて靴は相対的に安くなった。買手は相対的に安くなった財へ移るので、靴の需要は右へシフトする。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.6 (code 9911)

questions.stem: Y and Z are substitute goods. What would cause a shift in the supply curve to the right for Y, a normal good?

choices.label: A
choices.text: An increase in the price paid for Z.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cost-saving technological improvements in the production process for Z.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An expected increase in the future price of Y.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cost-saving technological improvements in the production process for Y.

questions.explanation: A supply curve shifts when the cost of producing that same good changes. Cheaper technology in Y's own production lowers its cost at every level of output, so more Y is offered at each price. Anything happening to Z, or an expected future price, would move a different curve.
questions.explanationJa: 供給曲線がシフトするのは、その財自身の生産コストが変わるときである。Y自身の生産技術が安価になれば、どの産出水準でもコストが下がるので、各価格でより多くのYが供給される。Zに起きる事柄や将来価格の予想は、別の曲線を動かす要因である。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.7 (code 7149)

questions.stem: The market for product A is elastic and purely competitive. If the market price of product A increases, what is the effect on total revenue?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreases

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increases

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cannot be determined from the information given.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Remains the same.

questions.explanation: With elastic demand, the percentage fall in quantity exceeds the percentage rise in price, so price times quantity declines. Total revenue therefore falls. The rule is general: when demand is elastic, price and total revenue move in opposite directions.
questions.explanationJa: 需要が弾力的な場合、数量の減少率が価格の上昇率を上回るので、価格 × 数量は減少する。したがって総収入は減る。これは一般則であり、需要が弾力的であれば価格と総収入は逆方向に動く。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.8 (code 9911)

questions.stem:
Below is the demand schedule for Kendall tomatoes. Quantity Demanded by
Price | Michael | Kevin | Gabriel
$4.00 | 1 | 2 | 0
$3.50 | 2 | 4 | 0
$3.00 | 3 | 6 | 2
$2.50 | 4 | 8 | 5
Michael, Kevin, and Gabriel are the only buyers of Kendall tomatoes. Which of the following sets of prices and levels of output would be on the market demand curve?
questions.explanation: Market demand is the horizontal sum of the individual demands at each price. At $4.00 the three buyers want 1 + 2 + 0 = 3 units, and at $3.00 they want 3 + 6 + 2 = 11. Choice C states both pairs correctly. For reference, $3.50 gives 6 units and $2.50 gives 17.
questions.explanationJa: 市場需要は、各価格における個人の需要を水平方向に合計したものである。$4.00 では3人の需要が 1 + 2 + 0 = 3単位、$3.00 では 3 + 6 + 2 = 11単位となる。選択肢Cはこの2組をいずれも正しく示している。参考までに $3.50 では6単位、$2.50 では17単位である。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.9 (code 9911)

questions.stem: An improvement in technology that in turn leads to improved worker productivity would most likely result in

choices.label: A
choices.text: Wage decreases.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Wage increases.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A shift to the right in the supply curve and a lowering of the price of the output.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A shift to the left in the supply curve and a lowering of the price of the output.

questions.explanation: Higher productivity means the same inputs yield more output, so the cost of each unit falls and producers offer more at every price: the supply curve shifts right. With demand unchanged, the new equilibrium comes at a lower price. Wages are set in the labour market and are not determined by this shift.
questions.explanationJa: 生産性の向上とは、同じ投入からより多くの産出が得られることなので、1単位当たりのコストが下がり、生産者はどの価格でもより多く供給する。すなわち供給曲線が右へシフトする。需要が変わらなければ、新しい均衡は低い価格で成立する。賃金は労働市場で決まるものであり、このシフトによって決まるわけではない。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.10 (code 9911)

questions.stem: An increase in the market supply of coffee would result in a(n)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase in the price of coffee.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease in the demand for coffee.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase in the price of tea.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase in the quantity of coffee demanded.

questions.explanation: More supply pushes the price of coffee down, and buyers respond by moving down along their demand curve, so the quantity demanded rises. Note the wording: demand itself does not increase, only the quantity demanded at the new, lower price.
questions.explanationJa: 供給が増えればコーヒーの価格は下がり、買手は需要曲線に沿って下方へ移動するので、需要量が増える。言い回しに注意したい。需要そのものが増えるのではなく、新しい低い価格における需要量が増えるのである。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.11 (code 9911)

questions.stem: In any competitive market, an equal decrease in both demand and supply can be expected to always

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease both price and market-clearing quantity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase both price and market-clearing quantity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Decrease market-clearing quantity

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decrease price.

questions.explanation: Both shifts pull quantity the same way, so the market-clearing quantity certainly falls. On price they work against each other: falling demand pushes it down while falling supply pushes it up, so the net effect cannot be signed even when the shifts are equal in the diagram.
questions.explanationJa: 2つのシフトはいずれも数量を同じ方向へ動かすので、均衡取引量は確実に減少する。価格については互いに逆に働く。需要の減少は価格を押し下げ、供給の減少は押し上げるので、図の上で同じ幅のシフトであっても、正味の効果の符号は定まらない。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.12 (code 9911)

questions.stem: If a legal price floor of $5.00 is declared given the situation illustrated in the accompanying diagram, what will be the result? The diagram plots price per gallon against quantity for milk. Supply and demand cross at $3.50 and 70,000 gallons. At a price of $5.00 the quantity supplied is 80,000 gallons while the quantity demanded is 60,000 gallons.

choices.label: A
choices.text: A surplus of 20,000 gallons.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A shortage of 20,000 gallons.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A shortage of 10,000 gallons.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A surplus of 10,000 gallons.

questions.explanation: A price floor above equilibrium leaves sellers wanting to sell more than buyers will take. At $5.00 the quantity supplied is 80,000 gallons against 60,000 demanded, so the excess is a surplus of 20,000 gallons. A shortage would arise only from a ceiling set below the $3.50 equilibrium.
questions.explanationJa: 均衡を上回る下限価格のもとでは、売手が売りたい量が買手の引き取る量を上回る。$5.00 では供給量80,000ガロンに対し需要量は60,000ガロンなので、差の20,000ガロンが余剰となる。不足が生じるのは、均衡価格 $3.50 を下回る上限価格が設定された場合だけである。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.13 (code 9911)

questions.stem: In the economic theory of production and cost, the short run is defined to be a production process

choices.label: A
choices.text: Which spans a time period of less than 3 months in length.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In which all inputs employed are variable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: That is subject to economies of scale.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In which both fixed and variable inputs are employed.

questions.explanation: The short run is defined by the presence of at least one input that cannot be varied, typically plant and equipment, so output is changed by adjusting the variable inputs around that fixed capacity. It is not a fixed length of calendar time, and the long run is the period in which every input becomes variable.
questions.explanationJa: 短期とは、変更できない投入が少なくとも一つ存在する期間として定義される。通常は設備や工場がこれにあたり、その固定された能力の周りで可変的な投入を調整して産出を変える。暦の上での特定の長さを指すものではなく、すべての投入が可変になる期間が長期である。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.14 (code 9911)

questions.stem: All of the following are true about perfect competition except that

choices.label: A
choices.text: Firms are price takers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There are a large number of buyers and sellers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: There is a standardized product.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the long run, an increase in profit will have no effect on the number of firms in the market.

questions.explanation: Free entry and exit is exactly what perfect competition assumes, so profit above the normal level attracts new firms until it is competed away. Saying profit has no effect on the number of firms describes a market with barriers, not a competitive one. The other three are core assumptions.
questions.explanationJa: 参入・退出の自由はまさに完全競争が前提とするところであり、正常水準を超える利潤は新規参入を招き、競争によって消えるまで企業数が増える。利潤が企業数に影響しないというのは、参入障壁のある市場の説明であって競争市場のものではない。他の3つは中核的な前提である。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.15 (code 9911)

questions.stem: All of the following are characteristics of monopolistic competition except that

choices.label: A
choices.text: The firms sell a homogeneous product.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The firms tend not to recognize the reaction of competitors when determining prices.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Firms tend to earn normal profits.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Price is higher than in pure competition.

questions.explanation: Monopolistic competition is defined by differentiated products: each seller offers something buyers see as distinct, which is what gives it a little pricing power and lets price exceed the pure competition level. A homogeneous product is the assumption of pure competition.
questions.explanationJa: 独占的競争は製品の差別化によって定義される。各売手は買手が別物と認識するものを提供しており、それがわずかな価格決定力を与え、価格を純粋競争の水準より高くする。同質の製品を前提とするのは純粋競争である。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.16 (code 9911)

questions.stem: An industry that is oligopolistic would be best characterized by

choices.label: A
choices.text: Many firms selling unique products.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A single firm selling a unique product.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Significant barriers to entry.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Horizontal or flat demand curves for the output of individual firms.

questions.explanation: An oligopoly has few sellers, and it stays that way because entry is hard: scale economies, capital requirements, or control of distribution keep newcomers out. Many firms with unique products is monopolistic competition, one firm is a monopoly, and a flat firm demand curve belongs to pure competition.
questions.explanationJa: 寡占は売手が少数であり、その状態が続くのは参入が難しいからである。規模の経済、必要資本、流通の押さえ込みが新規参入者を締め出す。多数の企業が独自製品を売るのは独占的競争、1社であれば独占、企業ごとの需要曲線が水平になるのは純粋競争である。
references: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト
questions.source: Proactive BAR Microeconomics テキスト Q.17 (code 9911)

questions.stem: Which one of the following examples best depicts the law of diminishing returns?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A small furnace is less efficient than a large furnace.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A manufacturing company purchases its supplier of materials.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At the No-Place-Like-Home restaurant, four cooks can prepare 160 meals in an evening while 3 cooks can prepare 150 meals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: John's Landscaping can mow an acre in 10 minutes and 2 acres in 15 minutes.

questions.explanation: Diminishing returns means each additional unit of a variable input adds less output than the one before. Three cooks average 50 meals each, but the fourth adds only 10, because the kitchen is fixed. Choice A is about scale, B is vertical integration, and D shows increasing returns.
questions.explanationJa: 収穫逓減とは、可変投入を1単位追加するごとに、その増加分が前の1単位より小さくなることをいう。3人の料理人は1人当たり50食だが、4人目は10食しか増やさない。厨房が固定されているからである。選択肢Aは規模の問題、Bは垂直統合、Dは収穫逓増の例である。

questions.stem: A corporation's net income as presented on its income statement is usually

choices.label: A
choices.text: Less than its economic profits because opportunity costs are considered in calculating net income.

choices.label: B
choices.text: More than its economic profits because economists consider interest payments to be costs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Equal to its economic profits.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Higher than its economic profits because opportunity costs are not considered in calculating net income.

questions.explanation: Accounting net income deducts only the explicit costs actually paid. Economic profit deducts implicit costs as well, chiefly the return the owner's own capital and labour could have earned elsewhere, so it is the smaller figure and accounting income is the higher one.
questions.explanationJa: 会計上の当期純利益は、実際に支払われた明示的費用だけを控除する。経済的利潤はこれに加えて暗黙的費用、とりわけ所有者自身の資本と労働が他で得られたはずの収益も控除するので、経済的利潤の方が小さく、会計上の利益の方が高くなる。

questions.stem: The competitive model of supply and demand predicts a long-run shortage only when

choices.label: A
choices.text: Maximum price is set above the equilibrium price.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maximum price is set below the equilibrium price.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Minimum price is set above the equilibrium price.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Minimum price is set below the equilibrium price.

questions.explanation: A shortage persists only when the price is held below the level that would clear the market, which is a maximum price, or ceiling, set below equilibrium. A ceiling above equilibrium does not bind, and a floor above equilibrium produces a surplus instead.
questions.explanationJa: 不足が続くのは、市場を均衡させる水準より低いところに価格が押さえられている場合だけであり、それは均衡を下回る上限価格である。均衡を上回る上限価格は拘束力を持たず、均衡を上回る下限価格はむしろ余剰を生む。

A monopolist tends to, in comparison with firms in a perfectly competitive market
Produce | Sell at

choices.text: Same | Higher

choices.label: B
choices.text: More | Higher Price

choices.label: C
choices.text: Less | Lower

choices.label: D
choices.text: Less | Higher Price

questions.explanation: A monopolist faces the whole market demand curve, so selling more requires cutting the price on every unit and marginal revenue falls below price. It therefore stops at a smaller output than a competitive industry would, and charges more for it: less output at a higher price.
questions.explanationJa: 独占企業は市場需要曲線の全体に直面するので、より多く売るにはすべての単位について価格を下げなければならず、限界収入は価格を下回る。したがって競争的な産業より少ない産出量で生産を止め、それをより高い価格で売る。すなわち産出は少なく価格は高い。

questions.stem: Companies in monopolist and monopolistic competitive markets maximize profits when

choices.label: A
choices.text: Average costs are minimized

choices.label: B
choices.text: Marginal cost equals marginal revenue

choices.label: C
choices.text: Price equals marginal costs

choices.label: D
choices.text: Where total revenue is maximized

questions.explanation: Profit is maximized where marginal cost equals marginal revenue, and that holds in every market structure. What differs is that a firm with pricing power has marginal revenue below its price, so it stops short of the point where price equals marginal cost.
questions.explanationJa: 利潤が最大になるのは限界費用と限界収入が等しくなる点であり、これはどの市場構造でも成り立つ。異なるのは、価格決定力を持つ企業では限界収入が価格を下回るため、価格と限界費用が一致する点には達しないところで止まる点である。

questions.explanation: Marginal physical product is the extra output from one more worker, measured in units: going from 20 to 21 workers raises output from 40 to 45, so the marginal physical product is 5 units. The 45 in choice D is the new total, not the increment.
questions.explanationJa: 限界物的生産物とは、労働者を1人増やしたことによる産出の増加分を数量で測ったものである。20人から21人へ増やすと産出は40から45へ増えるので、限界物的生産物は5単位となる。選択肢Dの45は増加分ではなく増加後の総量である。

20 | 40 | $75.00
21 | 45 | $69.00
22 | 48 | $67.50
The marginal revenue per unit when one worker is added to a team of 21 workers is
questions.explanation: Work in total revenue. With 21 workers, 45 units sell at $69.00 for $3,105; with 22 workers, 48 units sell at $67.50 for $3,240. Revenue rises $135 while output rises 3 units, so marginal revenue per unit = $135 / 3 = $45.00. It falls well below the $67.50 price because selling more forced the price down on every unit.
questions.explanationJa: 総収入で考える。21人では45単位が $69.00 で売れて $3,105、22人では48単位が $67.50 で売れて $3,240。収入は $135 増え、産出は3単位増えるので、単位当たり限界収入 = $135 ÷ 3 = $45.00。販売価格 $67.50 を大きく下回るのは、より多く売るために全単位の価格を下げたためである。

20 | 40 | $75.00
21 | 45 | $69.00
22 | 48 | $67.50
The marginal revenue product when one worker is added to a team of 21 workers is
questions.explanation: The marginal revenue product is the whole increase in revenue that the extra worker brings in: $3,240 - $3,105 = $135.00. That is the most the firm could pay that worker. It differs from marginal revenue per unit, which spreads the same $135 over the 3 additional units.
questions.explanationJa: 限界収入生産物とは、追加した労働者がもたらす収入の増加額そのものである: $3,240 − $3,105 = $135.00。これがその労働者に支払いうる上限である。同じ $135 を追加の3単位に割り振った単位当たり限界収入とは別の概念である。

The total cost of producing seven units is
questions.explanation: Total cost = average total cost x quantity. At seven units the average total cost is $39.29, so total cost = 7 x $39.29 = $275.03. Choice D, $296.00, is the total at eight units (8 x $37.00), and multiplying the average variable cost instead would give $175.00.
questions.explanationJa: 総費用 = 平均総費用 × 数量。7単位における平均総費用は $39.29 なので、総費用 = 7 × $39.29 = $275.03。選択肢Dの $296.00 は8単位の総費用（8 × $37.00）であり、平均変動費を掛けると $175.00 になる。

questions.explanation: Marginal cost is the change in total cost, so build both totals first: 9 units cost 9 x $35.36 = $318.24 and 8 units cost 8 x $37.00 = $296.00. The ninth unit therefore costs $318.24 - $296.00 = $22.24. Reading the average total cost of $35.36 as the marginal cost is the trap in choice D.
questions.explanationJa: 限界費用は総費用の変化額なので、まず両方の総費用を求める: 9単位は 9 × $35.36 = $318.24、8単位は 8 × $37.00 = $296.00。したがって9単位目の費用は $318.24 − $296.00 = $22.24。平均総費用 $35.36 をそのまま限界費用と読むのが選択肢Dの罠である。
